pull_request_body:
## Why

This is a focused follow-up to the render-scale transition work in
[PR #41](https://github.com/ParticleTroned/skyrim-community-shaders/pull/41),
[PR #43](https://github.com/ParticleTroned/skyrim-community-shaders/pull/43),
and [PR #44](https://github.com/ParticleTroned/skyrim-community-shaders/pull/44).

Two paths still did unnecessary or overly broad work:

- `ShaderCache::ServicePendingDisable()` resolved render-scale controller
  status on every enabled stable frame, although native-target restoration is
  only relevant after a deferred disable request.
- After the prepared-provider handoff in PR #44, an in-world CS-menu overlay
  could still be withheld while a replacement was merely queued, even if the
  submitted original and the retained stereo generation were exact.

The fix must retain the present device-loss, native-restoration, resource
identity, generation, and lifecycle protections. It must not turn an
unmeasured internal reduction into a performance claim.

## What changed

### Stable shader-cache frames

- Restore the atomic pending-disable fast path. A stable enabled frame stops
  after reading `pendingDisableAfterVRNativeRestore`; it no longer resolves
  render-scale status.
- A real deferred disable still checks native-target restoration before
  disabling the shader cache, and re-enabling still cancels the pending
  request.

### CS-menu presentation during a queued relatch

- Permit the in-world CS-menu overlay only after the existing stereo packet
  proves the exact current engine source, D3D11 device, descriptor, bounds,
  resource revision, generation, retained resource ownership, and a matching
  both-eye vendor-presentation generation.
- Limit that exception to a queued render-scale transition and/or queued
  render-target recreate. It does not bypass the existing upscaler dispatch
  or construct a replacement resource set.
- Keep the admission policy self-contained and make its exhaustive policy
  test independently calculate the allowed reason mask. The test therefore
  detects an accidental future widening of the policy.

## Relation to earlier work and evidence

This PR deliberately reuses prior mechanisms rather than introducing another
transition controller or resource-lifetime scheme.

| Related PR | Reused contract | Relevant recorded evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [#41](https://github.com/ParticleTroned/skyrim-community-shaders/pull/41) | Compact presentation contract and strongly owned stereo packet | Its controlled Save 14 run completed 20/20 transitions with no transition/OOM/device-loss failures and measured effectively flat steady-state submit cost. |
| [#43](https://github.com/ParticleTroned/skyrim-community-shaders/pull/43) | Current runtime-FSR, HAM, mirror, FOV, and Periphery-TAA pipeline | Its paired in-game A/B had no material pooled mean change; both runs improved GPU and CPU P95. PR #45 changes none of those GPU paths. |
| [#44](https://github.com/ParticleTroned/skyrim-community-shaders/pull/44) | Prepared resource and proven-provider handoff | It records the observed `4 -> 0 -> 4` menu quality sequence and keeps a valid provider authoritative while an exact replacement is prepared. This PR only admits the final CS-menu overlay in that already-proven pre-mutation state. |

The linked results are evidence for those prerequisite contracts, not runtime
measurements claimed for this PR.

### Manual in-game issue discovery

The tester ran repeated Skyrim VR sessions with the same mod list and settings
while the in-game profiler toggle was off. The supplied Community Shaders logs
and visual observations identified the remaining handoff issue:

- Closing the CS menu could visibly pass through `4 -> 0 -> 4` before the
  high-quality provider recovered. During that period, quick turns stuttered
  and elevated frame times did not recover promptly.
- PR #44 substantially improved the transition, and subsequent testing found
  door transitions smooth again. This narrowed the remaining fault from the
  general load/door path to presentation while a CS-menu replacement remains
  queued.
- The manual runs motivated the exact pre-mutation admission rule in this PR:
  retain an already proven generation; do not relax device, lifecycle, or
  physical-mutation guards.

These observations are qualitative troubleshooting evidence, not a controlled
frame-time benchmark. A final comparison still needs matched external SteamVR
frame timing or Tracy captures with identical scene, pose, settings, and warm
shader cache. PR #45 therefore makes no measured performance claim.

## Safety and failure behavior

Admission remains fail-closed for:

- D3D device loss, post-load reset, active physical target mutation, native
  restoration, unsafe source identity, invalid descriptor/bounds, and stale
  packet/resource generation.
- Pending runtime reset, pending vendor-runtime reset, and unknown or future
  suppression-reason bits.
- A missing, inactive, non-vendor, mismatched, or incompletely owned stable
  stereo generation.

When proof fails, the hook retains its existing suppression/fallback behavior;
this PR does not synthesize a successful compositor submission. Normal stable
frames do not enter the packet-proof path, and no shader, provider, D3D11
resource, setting, or DevBench surface is added.

## Scope and compatibility

The production change is VR-only at the OpenVR submit boundary plus the shared
shader-cache pending-disable service. It leaves SE/AE behavior unchanged and
does not change render scale, FOV, runtime-FSR, HAM, mirror, Periphery-TAA, or
resource-prewarm policy introduced by the related PRs.

## Validation

### PR #45 checks

- Passed: `pwsh ./tools/git.ps1 diff --check origin/main-VR...HEAD`.
- Passed: `git show --check` for each of the three commits in this PR.
- Passed before the third policy-only follow-up commit: focused VS2026
  `cl.exe` compilation with `/std:c++latest /W4 /WX` and execution of
  `overlay_policy_test` and `shader_cache_disable_policy_test`.

### Not run for the third commit

Per the requested no-build/no-test iteration, the focused policy executables
were not recompiled after `e001b4c38`. A full VS2026 build, shader validation,
pre-commit hooks, DevBench capture, and in-game VR validation were also not
run for this PR.

The related PR links above contain their own exact build and controlled
in-game evidence. They are not represented as validation of this final diff.

fix(vr): bound temporal culling recovery (#46)

* fix(vr): bound temporal culling recovery

Skyrim VR consumes native OBB occlusion results one frame after they are produced. PR 17 made every occluded object visible after head motion, while PR 27 removed that costly blanket fallback.

Restore view-coherence validation with a Balanced default that derives conservative bounds from the existing CPU OBB data and promotes at most 64 high-risk objects. Add an opt-in Performance Mode that accepts native stale results, keep all depth-culling controls together, and restore interior culling in fresh defaults.

Expose the policy and counters through DevBench, cover the pure selection policy with a controller test, and preserve the reverse-engineering and validation evidence in development documentation.

* fix(vr): harden temporal recovery

Make Performance Mode return before consumer-side camera and motion
work, and leave native results unchanged when no valid producer pose
exists.

Build the motion envelope once per miss, include translation in the
rotational bound, derive conservative bounds for non-orthogonal axes,
and select the bounded candidate set with a fixed heap.

Use alias-safe reads for the reverse-engineered culler layout, keep
performance measurements deterministic, remove incidental formatting
churn, and record current-head validation limits.

* fix(vr): finalize temporal culling recovery

Keep the temporal controller dormant while native depth culling is off and
require a new producer pose when it is re-enabled. This avoids recovery
work outside the active feature path and prevents a new result stream from
using a pose captured during an earlier enabled interval.

Expose the effective culling state through DevBench for trustworthy A/B
runs. Rename the current-head ShaderCache local that shadows its member so
the Release build is warning-clean under C4458-as-error.

pull_request_body:
## Why

Skyrim VR consumes the OBB depth-culling readback one frame after the
producing pose. Native occluded results can therefore be stale when the HMD
moves.

[PR 17](https://github.com/ParticleTroned/skyrim-community-shaders/pull/17)
addressed the missing-geometry fault by promoting every occluded result while
the view changed. Its implementation and hardening landed in
[42e94d0](https://github.com/ParticleTroned/skyrim-community-shaders/commit/42e94d004c4a420b2350c597bae162f28c88b61e)
and
[348e37b](https://github.com/ParticleTroned/skyrim-community-shaders/commit/348e37b7e5a71420fbcc7dbc71ece406ea9b8189).
The original physical-HMD reproduction and fix evidence is preserved in the
[PR 17 validation note](https://github.com/ParticleTroned/skyrim-community-shaders/blob/42e94d004c4a420b2350c597bae162f28c88b61e/docs/development/vr-depth-culling-temporal-validity.md).

That promote-all fallback avoided the visual fault, but a PR 16 versus PR 17
A/B reported about 1 ms lower frame time plus noisier CPU and GPU frame times.

[PR 27](https://github.com/ParticleTroned/skyrim-community-shaders/pull/27)
then removed the temporal hook in
[72f6e84](https://github.com/ParticleTroned/skyrim-community-shaders/commit/72f6e84ab1e40a0185fabbd92929627e55cd753c)
and changed the fresh interior default. That restored the lower-cost native
path, but also restored the one-frame visibility risk.

This PR supplies a bounded middle ground without a synchronous GPU readback.
The investigation started from the
[PR 43 test baseline](https://github.com/ParticleTroned/skyrim-community-shaders/pull/43).
Exact Ghidra symbols, live Skyrim VR 1.4.15 layout observations, commands,
results, and validation limits are preserved in the
[evidence record](https://github.com/ParticleTroned/skyrim-community-shaders/blob/07930ade6d20636d5415a2a043aa98e0de5e10fc/docs/development/vr-depth-culling-temporal-evidence.md).

## What changed

- Balanced is the default. Coherent frames keep the native result. On a valid
  envelope miss, CSX reads the existing CPU OBB transforms, derives
  conservative bounds, expands them for measured head translation and
  rotation, retests them against the current camera frustum, and promotes at
  most 64 high-risk occluded objects.
- Candidates already visible in the current frustum rank first. Remaining
  candidates rank by native angular coverage with deterministic index
  tie-breaking.
- Performance Mode returns from the consumer hook before camera lookup,
  motion analysis, OBB scanning, or result mutation. Producer-pose capture
  stays active while culling is enabled, so switching back to Balanced is
  immediately valid.
- When native depth culling is inactive, both temporal hooks return before
  pose capture, camera work, OBB scanning, or result writes. Re-enabling
  culling waits for one new producer pose before Balanced recovery resumes.
- DevBench reports settings, mode, effective culling state, and recovery
  counters. Its `set_depth_culling_performance_mode` action requires a
  boolean `enabled` for controlled same-build A/B runs.
- The compact Depth Culling UI keeps exterior culling, interior culling,
  Performance Mode, and Min Occludee Box Extent together, with focused
  tooltips in both existing settings locations.
- Interior depth culling defaults to enabled for fresh settings. An explicitly
  saved disabled value remains disabled.
- Performance measurement capture/restore includes the temporal mode and
  chooses deterministic Balanced/native states for its two phases.
- The current `main-VR` C4458 blocker is fixed by renaming the local
  `enableRequested` value in `ShaderCache::ServicePendingDisable`; it no
  longer shadows the member and has no behavior change.
- The durable behavior is documented in the
  [policy note](https://github.com/ParticleTroned/skyrim-community-shaders/blob/07930ade6d20636d5415a2a043aa98e0de5e10fc/docs/development/vr-depth-culling-temporal-policy.md).

## Adversarial review fixes

Review against current `main-VR` found and corrected these issues:

- Performance Mode still performed consumer-side camera and motion work.
- Recovery could run while native depth culling was disabled. It is now
  explicitly dormant and DevBench reports the effective state.
- Re-enabling culling could reuse a pose from an earlier enabled interval.
  A culling epoch requires a fresh producer pose before recovery.
- A missing producer pose was treated as a 180-degree miss and could trigger
  an unnecessary first-frame recovery.
- Combined translation and rotation omitted translation from the rotational
  radius, so the envelope was not fully conservative.
- Constant envelope terms were recomputed for every object instead of once
  per miss.
- The original bounded selector could perform 4,096 x 64 comparisons. It is
  now a fixed-capacity heap with O(n log 64) selection and no allocation.
- The original sphere derivation assumed orthogonal axes. It now evaluates
  the signed-axis extrema and remains conservative for non-orthogonal input.
- Raw reverse-engineered fields were read through typed aliasing casts. They
  now use named offsets and `memcpy`-based trivially-copyable reads.
- Current head promoted C4458 to an error because a ShaderCache local shadowed
  a member. The local is now explicitly named `enableStillRequested`.
- Whole-file formatting had changed unrelated VR and menu lines. That churn
  was removed from the final base diff.

No existing top-N helper or equivalent temporal policy was present in the
repository, so the fixed-capacity selector remains local to this concern.

## Safety and failure behavior

- Hooks install only on Skyrim VR 1.4.15 and only while both relocation sites
  contain CALL instructions.
- The render hook chains through the current call target, preserving the
  existing optional FrameAnnotations wrapper.
- Missing or out-of-epoch producer poses, non-finite motion, invalid counts
  or selectors, null native buffers, malformed transforms, and expansion
  overflow leave native results unchanged. At most 4,096 objects are
  inspected.
- Balanced can promote no more than 64 objects per miss. Individual draw cost
  remains scene-dependent, but PR 17's unbounded promote-all behavior cannot
  recur.
- No synchronous readback, shader replacement, dispatch, or D3D resource is
  added. SE and AE paths are unchanged.
- Performance Mode deliberately retains the native one-frame artifact risk;
  the UI and documentation state that tradeoff.

## Validation

Current base:

- `origin/main-VR`: `9daec10c706d56916bfb69782c872926aa90fbfb`
- Merge base equals that commit; the branch is not behind current head.

Passed:

- `pwsh ./tools/cmake.ps1 --build --preset CSmain -- /m:1`: Release
  `CommunityShaders.dll` built successfully.
- `pwsh ./tools/cmake.ps1 --build build/ALL --config Release --target
  controller_tests -- /m:1`
- `ctest --test-dir build/ALL -C Release -L ControllerTests
  --output-on-failure --timeout 300`: 27/27 passed.
- Final focused `VRDepthCullingTemporalPolicy` rebuild and test: passed.
- Pinned Prettier on the changed documentation and pinned clang-format
  dry-run checks on the final changed C++ ranges: passed.
- `git diff --check origin/main-VR...HEAD`: passed.
- GitHub feature-version audit: no actionable suggestions.

The normal post-build step staged the built DLL and PDB into the configured
AIO package location. It did not create an archive or deploy to Skyrim/MO2.

Not run:

- No headset visual or frame-time A/B was run for this branch.
- Shader tests were disabled because this PR changes no HLSL. The earlier
  shader-enabled configure was also blocked by the local
  ShaderTestFramework/NuGet SSL setup.
- The full-file clang-format hook was not kept because it rewrites

fix(upscaling): own DLSS evaluations (#47)

Bind each Streamline evaluation to its numeric frame token,
viewport, and session epoch.

Compare complete constants, resource identities, and rendered-input

Strongly own a reusable center output only after successful

Reject changed or incomplete same-token work without a second

pull_request_body:
## Why

The previous DLSS frame cache covered only part of the constants
contract and treated the FrameToken address as part of its identity.
An exact constants-cache hit could still reach slEvaluateFeature again,
and ordinary option-cache invalidation could erase the only local record
while Streamline still owned the numeric token.

That allowed repeated or changed work to reach one Streamline temporal
tuple and made completed-output ownership ambiguous. The DevBench trace
from b46edeaed exposes the relevant numeric token, constants, and evaluate
events, but remains diagnostic rather than production policy.

## What changed

- Add one bounded evaluation ticket keyed by Streamline session epoch,
  numeric token, resolved viewport, eye role, rendered-input generation,
  resource generation, exact extents, options, resources, and every
  canonical Streamline constant.
- Record constants and evaluation attempts and completion independently.
  No exact tuple can issue either provider call twice.
- Strongly own a reusable foveated-center output only after evaluation
  succeeds. Full-eye outputs remain non-reusable because later passes may
  sharpen, mask, or menu-composite them.
- Keep tickets across ordinary DLSS option-cache invalidation. Retire them
  on Streamline initialization, device replacement, teardown, or device
  loss.
- Advance submit-stage input generations on compositor cycles, source or
  render-contract changes, and changed foveated staging contracts.
- Bind existing finalized-eye and foveated-center fast caches to the same
  authoritative compositor/input generations.
- Add a compile-time controller policy test for first admission, exact
  owned reuse, partial and failed attempts, same-token conflicts, and
  independent temporal tuples.

## Safety and failure behavior

Changed input, constants, resources, eye role, or engine frame under an
already-used numeric token is rejected before another Streamline call.
The submit controller retains the token state and uses its established
stereo fallback path instead of resetting temporal history mid-tuple.

The ticket array is fixed at 16 entries and never allocates in the hot
path. It adds no textures, copies, locks, device queries, or permanent
VRAM. Strong ownership is limited to successfully completed center
outputs whose dependency graph is read-only until composition.

## Validation

Passed:

- pwsh ./tools/git.ps1 diff --cached --check
- pwsh ./tools/git.ps1 show --check --stat --oneline HEAD
- Clean feature-branch worktree after commit

Not run at user direction:

- Controller-test compilation or execution
- C++ build or shader validation
- Skyrim VR runtime and visual testing
- csx-render-scale-pr-v1 qualification and performance comparison

refactor(vr): gate idle render-scale work (#48)

* refactor(vr): gate idle render-scale work

Render callbacks previously entered both render-scale watchdogs even when no
relatch or recovery owner existed. Publish a compact maintenance wake mask
after each authoritative owner tuple so stable rendering needs one acquire
load and no watchdog calls, locks, or time queries.

Keep the queue flag and watchdog epochs authoritative. Consumers clear only
observed bits, recheck the corresponding owners, and re-arm active work so
concurrent publication cannot be lost. Preserve the existing render-thread
and compositor recovery service points, and cover all work-bit combinations
in the controller policy test.

* refactor(vr): preserve active maintenance bits

Keep wake bits published while their authoritative owner remains live so
transition frames avoid a clear-and-rearm atomic write pair and never
transiently hide active work.

Clear only stale observed bits, then recheck their owners and republish any
work that raced the clear.
pull_request_body:
## Why

`State::Draw` calls the render-target relatch service from a frequently
reached dirty-state callback. The prior empty path constructed a scope guard
and entered both render-scale watchdogs even when there was no relatch,
pre-mutation fallback, or post-mutation recovery to service.

Moving the scope guard behind only the relatch flag would be unsafe: the
post-mutation serialization owner can remain live after the relatch request
has been consumed. The optimization therefore needs a separate wake contract
that keeps watchdog liveness independent from queue lifetime.

This is the second independent render-scale follow-up after the DLSS
evaluation ownership work in #47. It is intentionally classified as a
refactor because the steady-path reduction has not yet been measured with a
matching in-game baseline.

## What changed

- Publish a compact three-bit maintenance hint for queued render-target
  relatches, pre-mutation fallback watchdogs, and post-mutation watchdogs.
- Publish each bit only after its complete authoritative queue or epoch tuple.
- Make stable `State::Draw` calls return after one acquire load, without
  watchdog calls, owner loads, locks, or monotonic time queries.
- Centralize active maintenance service and reconcile only the observed bits
  against the authoritative owners after service.
- Cover all eight maintenance-owner combinations in the existing
  `VRVendorRelatchPolicy` controller test.

## Safety and failure behavior

The maintenance mask is only a wake hint. The existing relatch flag and
watchdog epochs remain the authority for whether work may run.

Consumers clear an observed bit before rechecking its owner. Because every
publisher writes the owner before its release `fetch_or`, either the acquire
recheck sees concurrently published work or the publisher sets the bit after
the clear. A concurrent arm therefore cannot be lost.

The existing service opportunities are preserved:

- `State::Draw` services relatch, pre-mutation, and post-mutation work.
- `ConfigureUpscaling` retains its post-mutation-only watchdog opportunity.
- The post-load compositor hard deadline retains its CPU-only post-mutation
  service opportunity after releasing the compositor hold mutex.

No D3D work moves to the compositor path. No deadline, frame clock, recovery
policy, resource ownership, fallback, or image-quality behavior changes. A
bit publication racing an already-entered empty service turn is handled by
the next existing service opportunity without exposing a partial tuple.

## Validation

Passed on current `main-VR` with Visual Studio 2026:

- `pwsh ./tools/cmake.ps1 --build build/ALL --config Release --target vr_vendor_relatch_policy_test --parallel`
- `ctest --test-dir build/ALL -C Release -R '^VRVendorRelatchPolicy$' --output-on-failure`
  - 1/1 passed.
- `pwsh ./tools/cmake.ps1 --build --preset CSmain --parallel`
  - `CommunityShaders.dll` compiled and linked successfully.
- `pwsh ./tools/git.ps1 diff --check`

Not run:

- Shader tests, because this PR changes no HLSL or shader bindings.
- The repository commit hook, per the known local hook failure policy.

### `csx-render-scale-pr-v1`

Blocked before runtime mutation. This Codex session has no explicit
`CSX_DEVBENCH_RUNTIME_PATH`, completed fixture manifest, or accepted matching
baseline evidence directory/build ID. The DevBench controller contract
forbids searching an MO2 tree for substitutes, so no generated `pr-summary.md`
or runtime performance/fidelity verdict is claimed.

The PR remains draft until the exact candidate DLL is deployed and the
versioned PR qualification, baseline comparison, and nine-sample visual review
are completed. Missing evidence is not treated as a pass.

fix(vr): lease OpenVR submit resources (#49)

* fix(vr): lease submit textures

Retain the exact DirectX color and optional depth texture while OpenVR Submit runs, without holding the global render-target recreation mutex across the external compositor call.

Copy pose, bounds, flags, device identity, and resource generation into the packet. Revalidate after Submit and ignore stale success observations so a concurrent relatch cannot advance current presentation state.

* fix(vr): harden submit texture leases

Preserve the exact OpenVR texture payload and reject stale or unknown render-target publications without leaving compositor-hold bookkeeping active.

* docs(agents): carry RC166 lessons workflow

Rationale:
The first stacked topic branch predates the RC166 integration branch's workflow file. Without the same tree entry, retargeting the PR would appear to delete the branch-local agent rule and later stacked branches would not inherit it.

Implementation:
Add the identical RC166 lessons workflow to the topic branch so the PR preserves the base rule and every descendant branch receives the required commit, attribution, diagnostics, fidelity and adversarial-review constraints.

Validation:
Documentation-only tree reconciliation; no build or runtime validation was performed.

Provenance:
No external code was copied or directly adapted.
pull_request_body:
## Why

The OpenVR Submit hook held the global render-target recreation mutex while calling the external compositor. If NVIDIA/OpenVR blocked in `Submit`, render-target recreation could not acquire the exclusive side of the mutex, leaving render-scale relatching and other render-target work unable to progress.

This is item 1 of the stacked RC166-lessons series. It targets `codex/vr-renderscale-RC166lessons`; later items will be based on the reviewed head of this PR.

## What changed

- Capture an immutable OpenVR presentation packet while holding the render-target shared lock only long enough to copy and retain pointer-backed submission state.
- Copy the exact eye, flags, optional bounds, pose payload, depth payload, device identity and completed render-target publication generation.
- Retain the exact DirectX colour texture and optional depth texture with strong COM references; submitted handles are not substituted.
- Release the recreation lock before calling the original external OpenVR `Submit`.
- Revalidate device and publication generation after `Submit` and before success-dependent Community Shaders state is accepted.
- Treat a stale compositor success as an internal fail-closed result for post-load/presentation bookkeeping while preserving the real OpenVR result for the caller and diagnostics.
- Extend the existing overlay policy test target with lease-policy coverage rather than adding another controller executable.

## Invariants and failure behaviour

- No CSX global render-target recreation lock is held across the external OpenVR call.
- Strong COM ownership keeps colour/depth resources alive until the call returns.
- Existing stereo presentation packets remain responsible for longer both-eye render-scale lifetime and provenance.
- Invalid eyes, non-texture DirectX handles, wrong-device textures, missing required depth lifetime and missing completed publication generations fail closed.
- Non-DirectX submissions retain pass-through behaviour but cannot publish a current DirectX CSX presentation proof.
- A stale successful submission does not advance screenshot acceptance, render-scale presentation observations, native-restore ownership, post-load release bookkeeping or menu auto-hide state.
- SE/AE behaviour is unchanged and no new D3D resources are created.

## DevBench and diagnostics

The existing DevBench submit/load-presentation probe receives the retained packet identity and validity. A generation invalidation after the external call is represented as an internal failed completion rather than accepted presentation evidence. A transition-scoped debug line reports stale lease rejection with path, eye and generation; there is no per-frame production logging or new production polling.

## Adversarial review

The complete diff was reviewed against:

- external-call lock scope and lock-order inversion;
- exact COM interface/handle ownership;
- pose/depth flag combinations;
- wrong-device and missing-generation paths;
- generation changes during `Submit`;
- stale external success versus internal publication;
- first-eye/second-eye and retained native-peer handling;
- post-load keepalive and screenshot acceptance;
- non-DirectX pass-through;
- non-VR behaviour and absence of new D3D allocations.

The implementation deliberately does not weaken the existing stereo, native-restore, post-load or resource-publication contracts.

## Validation

- Passed previously: `pwsh ./tools/git.ps1 diff --check origin/main-VR`
- Passed previously: adversarial source review of lock scope, exact resource ownership, generation revalidation, failure paths and DRY scope
- Not yet run on the current stacked base: canonical Release DLL build and controller tests
- Not yet run: runtime/headset reproduction and render-scale qualification

The final validation section will be updated only with commands that actually run on this rebased stacked branch.

## Provenance

No external code was copied or directly adapted. The design is based on the repository's own render-target publication and lifetime contracts.

## Series dependency

- Base: `codex/vr-renderscale-RC166lessons`
- Series item: 1 / 12
- Next planned item: qualification milestones (`presentationStable` versus `cleanupDrained`)

fix(profiler): prevent nested total inflation

Feature timing totals summed every matching timer, so a parent scope and
its nested children counted the same GPU or CPU interval more than once.

and build feature, highlight, and global summary means from the same
frame-aligned accumulators. Mean-only summaries skip percentile sorting.

commit_message:
fix(tuning): stabilize cost measurements

Rationale:
Feature-cost runs could wait indefinitely for an unrealistically quiet
scene, treat optional GPU or CPU gaps as blockers, and present noisy or
overconfident results. Disjoint frame intervals could also be stitched
into one capture, weakening the A/B/A comparison.

Implementation:
Use bounded adjacent 500 ms averages before each exact three-second
A/B/A leg, then continue with a noisy-baseline warning at 2.25 seconds.
Exclude zero and invalid timing samples, restart only an interrupted leg,
and estimate SE/significance from weighted non-overlapping block means.
Present signed Game, FPS, GPU, and CPU results in a compact table and
omit percentile work from the right-hand profiler summary. Add focused
controller coverage for weighting, significance limits, invalid samples,
and timing discontinuities.

mixed-line-ending hooks.

Hover feedback resolved targets on every moving frame, and effect-mesh

Track dirty hover state behind a 50 ms refresh interval and silence both
collision and effect hover resolution. Resolve every flat or VR click fresh,
preserve frame-bounded VR click provenance, and emit one common log only
after a valid pick is committed.

Disabled or unloaded features leave their named passes in the profiler after

Track each timer's last sampled cycle with a saturating detailed-cycle counter.

commit_message:
fix(pbr): guard against mislinked texturesets (#2655)

Motivation:
Malformed meshes can link an arbitrary NetImmerse block through a
BSTextureSet field. Calling texture-set virtual methods on that object
can crash during the vanilla loader, PBR hashing, or texture mutation.

Rationale:
Validate the BSTextureSet NiRTTI hierarchy and fail closed before any
texture-set operation. Checking the base hierarchy rejects malformed
objects while retaining valid subclasses used by PBR decals.

Implementation:
Add a shared runtime-type predicate and retained-pointer cleanup helper.
Clear invalid incoming links before the base loader, validate retained
links before CRC queries and SetTexture calls, and preserve all existing
main-VR material behavior. The hierarchy predicate incorporates the
later #2666 correction so the narrower concrete-class regression is not
introduced.

Motivation:
The upstream 256 x 256 capture improves reflection detail but costs roughly
four times the capture and filtering work of the previous 128 x 128 path.
VR users need a bounded quality choice without maintaining another build.

Rationale:
Reflection resources are fixed during renderer startup, so the configured
resolution must be latched and every CPU and shader mip consumer must use
the active resource contract. main-VR therefore keeps 128 x 128 as the
default and makes 256 x 256 an explicit Quality choice.

Implementation:
Add Performance and Quality selectors, validate persisted values, and show
a restart warning when the configured value differs from the active
session. Derive resource and shader mip limits from the latched resolution,
reconcile release builds to the actual renderer target, and preserve the
existing VR capture cadence and foveation paths. Expose the configured and
active state through a non-persisting DevBench action and status payload.

pre-commit whitespace and line-ending hooks. clang-format and gersemi were
skipped because their whole-file rewrites churn baseline files. Reviewed

commit_message:
fix(menu): menu input lag and scroll granularity (#2668)

Motivation:
ImGui input trickling can backlog Skyrim's frame-sized input batches and
replay stale menu input, while Skyrim's wheel pseudo-buttons discard raw
DirectInput scroll granularity.

Rationale:
Consuming each complete batch prevents queue growth, and accumulating the
raw wheel delta preserves device resolution. The raw device read must be
isolated so a bad runtime pointer cannot suppress ordinary input handling.

Implementation:
Disable ImGui input trickling, capture and atomically accumulate the mouse
wheel delta, and submit its normalized value once per input cycle. Place
the device read in main-VR's existing structured-exception safeguard and
leave VR controller routing, input swallowing, and preview logic intact.

Validation:

line-ending hooks. clang-format and gersemi were skipped because their
whole-file rewrites churn baseline files. Compared the port against the
upstream and hardened SE implementations. Full build and runtime checks

fix(fog): lighting additive fog (#2677)

Motivation:
Additive lighting must blend against black. Applying the scene fog colour
first tints and brightens additive particles and lighting effects.

Rationale:
The normal fog factor should still attenuate additive geometry, but its fog
colour must be zero. Classifying the render pass from destination-one
alpha blending provides that distinction without another shader family.

Implementation:
Classify additive blend state before main-VR's existing lighting setup
hook, clear the descriptor on every pass, and suppress the vanilla or IBL
fog colour while retaining fog attenuation. Use descriptor bit 8 because
main-VR already reserves bits 6 and 7. Omit the absent Exponential Height
Fog integration and unrelated upstream formatting changes.

Validation:
Passed the staged diff check and scoped pre-commit whitespace and
line-ending hooks. clang-format and gersemi were skipped because their
whole-file rewrites churn baseline files. Verified matching C++ and HLSL
descriptor bits and the existing VR lighting-hook placement. Full build,
shader, and runtime checks are deferred until the end of the port series.

commit_message:
fix(tuning): refine feature cost measurements

Rationale:
Actual feature cost results need enough observations to absorb normal VR
frame variation without blocking Game and FPS when a small number of
compositor timings are unavailable. The UI also needs to distinguish
statistical significance from partial GPU or CPU coverage and prevent
immediate reruns before the restored state has settled.

Implementation:
Measure five equal-weight one-second intervals per state, wait nine
seconds before the Off/None capture, and enforce a ten-second post-run
cooldown. Calculate values and standard errors from the same block-mean
estimator, tolerate at most two missing GPU or CPU samples across both
states, mark partial rows with their exact count, and reject incomplete
or unsafe accumulations. Keep the results table compact and extend the
source test for interval weighting, coverage limits, and invalid input.

commit_message:
fix(wetterness): cache puddle noise (#63)

Rationale:
Procedural puddle masking evaluates up to two 3D Perlin functions per
eligible pixel. In-game A/B observations identified this path as a source
of frame-time instability, without a quantified GPU-time measurement.

Implementation:
Add cached Textured and High Quality masks plus a slope-only Simple mode,
retaining Legacy Procedural as an explicit compatibility option. Isolate
the generator and sampling helper under Wetterness-owned paths. Preserve
buffer size, migrate settings, and fall back to Simple on resource failure.
Document mode behavior and bump the feature shader contract to 1-7-1.

Validation:
Whitespace and patch-application checks passed against CSX main-VR.
The five-minute C++ build attempt stopped during CommonLib compilation.
Shader compilation and final in-game regression validation were not run.
pull_request_body:
## Why

Wetterness generates its puddle footprint with up to two 3D Perlin
evaluations per eligible pixel, including a layout-warp evaluation.
In-game A/B testing reported unstable frame times with this procedural
mask enabled. This change provides cheaper footprint generation without
changing the rest of the wetness or reflection model.

## What changed

- Add Simple, Textured, Textured High Quality, and Legacy Procedural
  puddle-mask modes. Textured is the default.
- Generate a deterministic 256 x 256, two-channel noise texture during
  resource setup. Textured uses one lookup; High Quality uses two.
- Keep the original procedural pattern available as an explicit option.
- Keep the mask generator and shader helper under Wetterness-owned paths.
- Add the selector to Puddles settings and the existing performance UI,
  with save/load, reset, and performance-state capture/restore support.
- Reuse the final per-frame padding lane for the mode. The buffer remains
  272 bytes and subsequent feature offsets are unchanged.
- Bump the Wetterness shader contract from 1-7-0 to 1-7-1.

This does not change Dynamic Cubemaps cadence, wet reflection blending,
direct-light evaluation, precipitation occlusion, grass, climate presets,
or the accumulation/drying model.

## Compatibility and failure behavior

Textured modes are an approximation and intentionally produce different
puddle layouts. Simple uses slope only, with no noise islands; Radius and
Layout have no effect in that mode.

Missing or out-of-range mode values select Textured. Prototype settings
using EnableProceduralPuddleNoise migrate to Simple when false and to
Textured when true, unless an explicit PuddleMaskMode is present.

Texture allocation/creation failure logs a warning and selects Simple for
rendering without overwriting the saved user choice. The menu reports the
fallback. Texture and view ownership use RAII, and both D3D resources are
named. No per-frame texture generation or new GPU pass is introduced.

The changed shader path is WETTERNESS-gated and shared by desktop and VR.
The DLL and shader package must be updated together.

## Validation

- Passed: git diff --check.
- Passed: isolated-index git apply --cached --check --whitespace=error-all
  against CSX main-VR c2542b11ecdc701ea34b3830f666387c0cf271f8.
- Passed: the edited baseline files are unchanged between the local base
  3d4199814b541d8ceba4dcac82fa9d7c7d17283d and that CSX tip.
- Formatting: changed ranges/new code formatted with clang-format 22.1.3.
- Passed: repository pre-commit checks on all eight staged files
  (whitespace, line endings, clang-format, and prettier).
- Incomplete: Release CommunityShaders-only build. CMake refreshed vcpkg
  dependencies; the five-minute watchdog terminated the build during
  CommonLib compilation before Wetterness compilation completed.
- Not run: shader compilation/validation, which requires explicit opt-in.
- Not run: in-game regression testing of this final cleaned patch.
- Earlier prototype A/B observations are the motivation, not validation
  of this final extraction. No quantified GPU-time saving is claimed.

Before merge: finish the C++ build, explicitly validate the relevant
shader permutations, and check the four modes in controlled desktop/VR
scenes, including rain, drying, shelters, shorelines, and camera movement.

fix(shader-cache): unify AIO cache ABI (#64) (#64)

* fix(shader-cache): unify AIO cache ABI

Rationale:
A universal AIO embeds one shader-cache ABI, but the cache builder
previously salted that ABI with the selected game runtime. One of the two
packaged runtime caches therefore missed every prebuilt record on first use.

Implementation:
Make the global shader ABI runtime-neutral while retaining runtime defines in
each record compile-state digest. Require both FOMOD cache inputs to match the
core build manifest ABI and cover the contract with focused regression tests.

* build(cache): validate FOMOD runtime slots

Rationale:
A runtime-neutral global shader ABI cannot detect an SE and VR cache
that was assigned to the wrong installer slot. Release assembly must
reject that mismatch before publication.

Implementation:
Validate the authoritative runtime metadata for source and staged cache
packs, report expected and observed values, and independently test ABI
authorities, wrong-slot inputs, malformed core metadata, and cleanup.

* build(cache): clarify ABI validation errors

Rationale:
Release metadata failures should identify the exact file, rejected
value, and required ABI form so maintainers can diagnose an invalid
candidate without additional inspection.

Implementation:
Report the core ABI value and type with its lowercase hexadecimal
requirement, use the exact Info.ini path for mismatches, and extend
focused rejection tests for every malformed ABI class.
pull_request_body:
## Why

The managed-cache release packages one universal DLL with separate SE/AE and
VR packs. The global shader-cache ABI nevertheless included the cache
builder's runtime, so the DLL could match only one packaged cache. The other
runtime missed every prebuilt record and compiled shaders on first startup.

## What changed

Make the global shader-cache ABI runtime-neutral and bump its identity schema.
SE and VR remain distinct in each record's compile-state digest, including the
existing `VR;` state for VR records.

Bind release assembly to the core's `CSX.BuildManifest.json`: both cache
`Info.ini` and `PackManifest.json` identities must match the core ABI. Each
pack manifest must also identify the runtime slot it is assigned to, so equal
global ABI values cannot make SE and VR release inputs interchangeable.

## Failure behavior

A missing, malformed, mismatched, or wrongly assigned core/cache identity now
fails FOMOD assembly before the candidate archive can replace the plain AIO.
Post-copy validation failures remove the candidate staging tree. Diagnostics
identify the exact metadata file and expected/observed ABI or runtime values.
Runtime source compilation remains the fallback for independently installed
incompatible caches.

## Validation

- Passed 32 focused provenance, FOMOD, and cache-packaging tests.
- Covered swapped/duplicated runtime inputs, independent `Info.ini` and
  `PackManifest.json` ABI mismatches, malformed core metadata and diagnostics,
  staged runtime mismatch, and post-copy cleanup.
- Passed scoped pre-commit for all changed files.
- Passed `git diff --check`.
- Verified both runtime record compile-state strings remain distinct.
- Independent re-review: `PASS_WITH_FINDINGS`; both prior findings resolved,
  with its final low diagnostic finding addressed in the latest commit.
- Not run: full shader-cache generation or in-game first-start smoke test.

commit_message:
fix(capture): harden dispatch and cleanup (#59)

* fix(capture): harden API scheduling

Rationale:
The screenshot API contract promises fair capture arbitration, bounded
render-thread work, attributable source acquisition, and complete journal
events. Automatic review established that the implementation did not yet
satisfy those integration guarantees.

Implementation:
Add bounded fair dispatch queues and round-robin sequence selection, move
sequence-manifest assembly to the worker through immutable child snapshots,
and retain source timing, plane, generation, and device provenance. Separate
capture-job capacity from source contention, complete packaging and source
events, enforce coherent stereo publications and shared path containment,
and extend focused contract and policy coverage.

* fix(capture): close dispatch lifecycle gaps

Rationale:
Single-eye multi-output requests could stage desktop captures, busy
dispatch attempts could starve manual requests and ignore sequence
backpressure policies, and cancellation could lose a child or report
success. Retiring long manifest chains could overflow the debug stack
and destroy the full snapshot under the render-path API lock.

Implementation:
Keep submitted-eye acquisition pending, alternate completed dispatcher
turns while retaining FIFO retries and deadlines, and reconcile parent
and child cancellation before finalization. Publish geometry fallback
only after capture admission and release partially started acquisitions
on dispatch exceptions. Retire immutable manifest snapshots on their
worker with iterative release. Add executable regressions for actual
Present and cancellation callbacks, arbitration, and shared snapshots.

---------

pull_request_body:
## Why

Screenshot API v1 needs fair bounded scheduling and durable capture
evidence. Concurrent requests could starve, source provenance was
incomplete, and large manifests could stall Present.

## What changed

- Alternate completed manual/sequence dispatch turns, retain manual FIFO
  order during bounded retries, and rotate sequence selection.
- Apply sequence `skip`/`abort` policies at the first source or encoder
  capacity miss; check dispatch deadlines before acquisition.
- Keep all requested same-eye outputs waiting for OpenVR Submit, including
  mixed raw/framed views, and require coherent stereo publication/device
  identity.
- Preserve requested/actual frame and timestamp identity, compositor cycle,
  source planes, bounds, orientation, colour and device provenance.
- Mark sequence and child cancellation before finalization, reconcile
  cancellation during dispatch, and release partially started captures
  when acquisition throws.
- Build and retire immutable manifest snapshots on the worker, releasing
  long chains iteratively.
- Publish acquisition, timeout, drop and packaging events at their state
  boundaries; publish geometry fallback only after capture admission.
- Report encoder capacity in capture jobs and use one containment rule for
  API settings, persisted settings, UI edits and folder opening.

## Adversarial review corrections

Review of `a6d591b6c5069fdea928c615861174ad4a3b1ab9` found and fixed:

| Severity | Trigger and previous failure |
| --- | --- |
| P1 | Multiple outputs from one eye could stage desktop pixels and fail instead of waiting for Submit. |
| P1 | Alternating every busy attempt could repeatedly give available slots to the same class; retrying at the tail also broke FIFO order. |
| P1 | Sequence capacity misses silently retried for ten seconds instead of honoring `skip`/`abort`. |
| P1 | Cancelling a popped request could strand it; disabling/shutting down a queued final child could report successful completion. |
| P2 | Pruning a long manifest destroyed the chain under the API lock; 10,000 children caused a debug stack overflow. |
| P2 | Busy retries could repeatedly publish geometry-fallback warnings for a capture that had not been admitted. |

## Runtime and failure behavior

The operation limit bounds admitted work. Manual source/encoder contention
retains its dispatch turn for at most ten seconds. Sequence misses are
recorded immediately. Cancellation removes reversible work while allowing
committed encoder artifacts to finish. Submitted-eye acquisition retains
its timeout and explicit fallback policy.

Native HMD execution remains an untested runtime gate.

## Validation

- Fix commit: `0409e97f7522cd82159ef0b3848c5ae1d0197216`.
- Base: `0ad1fc3f6ecaf5eb0313ae5508c23d0c39cd37a4`.
- Combined SE/AE/VR Release `CommunityShaders` and `controller_tests`
  build with DevBench enabled, MSVC 19.51 and `/W4 /WX`: passed.
  The final rebuild hit host paging-file exhaustion with unrestricted
  compiler parallelism; a process-local `_CL_=/MP4` retry passed.
- `ctest --test-dir C:/src/skyrim-community-shaders/build/pr59v -C Release --output-on-failure`:
  **50/50 passed** (49 controller tests plus ScreenshotApiContract).
- `ctest --test-dir C:/src/skyrim-community-shaders/build/pr59v -C Debug --output-on-failure -R "^Screenshot(ApiPolicy|ManifestSnapshot|CapturePresent|Dispatch)$"`:
  **4/4 passed**.
- Source-extracted Present and cancellation regressions fail against the
  original PR methods and pass against the fixed methods. The original
  10,000-child manifest chain reproduces `0xC00000FD` under `/Od`;
  iterative release passes Release and Debug, including shared checkpoints.
- Scoped C++/test pre-commit hooks and whitespace checks passed. New CMake
  blocks were formatted; whole-file Prettier/Gersemi for the existing large
  document/CMake file were skipped to avoid unrelated formatting changes.
- Logs: `C:/src/skyrim-community-shaders/build/pr59v/final-release-build.log`,
  `final-release-ctest.log`, `final-debug-build.log`,
  `final-debug-ctest.log`. The uncapped failure is retained separately.
- Validation DLL SHA-256:
  `8c245eea6f0d99226e2c95702d627279005e0f2610ced8e6d4fe29fa73783182`.
  Pinned dependencies were exported from local Git objects; their archive
  directories do not provide standalone Git provenance. This DLL is a
  validation artifact and was not deployed.
- Native live HMD capture was not run. GitHub build/shader checks are
  still running; WIP and the feature-version audit have passed.

commit_message:
fix(vr): prove stereo submit input freshness (#65)

* fix(vr): prove stereo submit input freshness

Rationale:
The submit path could encode, evaluate, replay, or reuse the unsubmitted
eye from a combined color texture while its depth and motion-vector guides
or source cycle were not proven current. That admitted stale peer data into
temporal vendor histories.

Implementation:
Correlate nested OpenVR submissions with the engine outer two-eye Submit
boundary and a completed current world frame, then bind caches to the exact
resource and region proof. Fall back to current-eye-only work whenever proof
or peer HMD-mask sanitation fails, preserve coherent foveated replay across
re-encoding, and add policy plus integration coverage.

* test(vr): capture freshness fixtures

Rationale:
Clang rejects captureless lambdas that copy local constexpr fixtures,
so the freshness policy target does not compile with Clang.

Implementation:
Capture boundary, admission, and proof by value in every test variant
while preserving the existing compile-time assertions.

* build(shaders): clear puddle mask compiler warnings

Rationale:
The full shader CI jobs reject FXC warnings in PuddleMask.hlsli,
including an unsupported pragma and definite-assignment analysis of the
legacy early-return path.

Implementation:
Use a standard include guard and explicit alternative control flow while
preserving every puddle calculation. Constant mask modes retain identical
DXBC; dynamic before/after shaders matched across 49,152 WARP comparisons.

* fix(vr): preserve exact submit input identity

Rationale:
Descriptor addresses do not establish continuity of the submitted D3D
resource. Rejected peer proofs also discarded safe same-eye work, and a
failed encode could leave stale preparation claims over modified guides.

Implementation:
Capture typed descriptor and resource identities at the outer boundary,
require resource continuity, and separate peer admission from scoped
same-eye reuse. Retain per-eye source ownership and invalidate claims
before writes, replacement, reset, and device loss. Expose fixed aggregate
DevBench outcomes and work counters. Add production composition coverage
for descriptor copies, mismatches, duplicate eyes, and failed replacement.

The three focused freshness tests pass. Live qualification remains pending
an available MO2 owner and a configured verified fixture.
pull_request_body:
## Why

The VR submit path could consume the unsubmitted eye from a combined
color texture without proving that its color, depth, motion vectors, and
producer cycle were current. Descriptor-address equality also admitted
changed resources and rejected copied descriptors of the same resource.

## What changed

- Capture outer and nested OpenVR descriptors through one typed extraction
  path. Match non-null DirectX resources independently of descriptor
  addresses, with exact token, cycle, frame, thread, and flags checks.
- Require a completed current world frame and exact source/region proof
  before peer encoding, stereo FSR dispatch, peer replay, or cache reuse.
- Retain independent same-eye preparation and finalized output within a
  correlated outer scope, including left/right/left submissions with
  separate sources. Keep source, depth, and motion-vector COM ownership.
- Retire preparation claims before attempted writes, including failed
  re-encoding, resource replacement, reset, and device loss.
- Expose fixed aggregate acceptance/rejection reasons and per-vendor work
  counters through `communityshaders.renderscale status.submitInputFreshness`.
- Add a production-facing composition test using real OpenVR descriptors,
  producer-proof construction, peer admission, and current-eye reuse.
- Repair the existing PuddleMask FXC warnings with an include guard and
  explicit branch control flow, without warning suppression.

## Safety and failure behavior

Rejected peer proof permits only the submitted eye. Its narrower reuse
identity cannot authorize peer reads, stereo dispatch, or peer history.
Missing outer scope disables reuse because in-place source rewrites cannot
be excluded. The repair remains in shared submit/policy code; NVIDIA vendor
implementation is unchanged.

The original pre-merge review did not run live qualification because its
fixture, matched baseline and test-profile preconditions were unavailable.
The post-merge NVIDIA tuning evidence below updates the runtime record;
no separate `csx-render-scale-pr-v1` qualification pass is claimed.

## Validation

### NVIDIA comparison: older baseline vs main-VR with PR65

**Main-VR averaged 799.2 ms per switch versus 834.3 ms for the older
baseline: 35.1 ms faster (4.2%).** The result varied between repeats:
repeat 1 was 10.2% faster than baseline; repeat 2 was 1.8% slower.
Recovered fidelity/vendor failures occurred in **all four main-VR
passes**, on the same two routes. The baseline had none.

All transitions completed and reached terminal PASS. The recurring
failures mean the main-VR result **does not meet the improvement-or-neutral
standard**, despite its lower combined average.

**Groups:** baseline = the two passes of the older renderer, compiled as
`390fdea25`; main-VR repeat 1 = two passes of `348803c18`; main-VR repeat
2 = two passes of `7c8e3e656`. Both main-VR builds include PR65. Repeat 2
adds retry instrumentation. The combined main-VR mean uses all four
passes equally; the baseline uses its two actual passes once.

#### Main comparison

Lower times are better. “Switch completion” means the strict waiter has
finished; “relatch proof” is the first exact new-generation proof.
The final two columns show **± one standard error (SE) across pass
summaries**, in the same units as the row.

<details>
<summary>How the means and SE are calculated</summary>

Mean = arithmetic mean of the retained pass summaries. SE = sample
standard deviation of those summaries divided by √n: n = 2 for the
baseline and each repeat, n = 4 for combined main-VR. Calculations use
unrounded values. SE is not a confidence interval or a significance test.

The four main-VR passes come from two process runs, with two ordered
passes in each. They are not four independent experiments. The requested
pass-based SE is descriptive. Using the two independent repeat means
instead gives a main-VR switch-time SE of **±50.3 ms**, compared with
**±30.8 ms** across the four pass means.

The baseline contains one process run with two passes; it was not rerun
for repeat 2. This grouping cannot establish a precise between-build
confidence interval. Different simulation times and instrumentation
also limit causal interpretation. It measures cumulative main-VR changes,
including PR65, rather than isolating this PR’s contribution.

</details>

fix(vr): preserve deferred FSR eye dispatch (#75)

* fix(vr): preserve deferred FSR eye dispatch

Rationale:
Cold runtime FSR resources can defer a valid single-eye evaluation.
Collapsing that wait into failure reports transient errors when producer
freshness prevents stereo batching and no compatible host is available.

Implementation:
Propagate the existing typed result through full-eye, foveated, main-pass,
and replay dispatch. Present deferred submits with ordinary stretch and
retain cycle ownership after intermediate recreation. Keep genuine
failures visible and reset history after partial eye completion. Reuse
host-fallback compatibility with the planned context count, add focused
production-function regression coverage, and record validation limits.
Builds, tests, and hooks remain unrun at the user's explicit direction.

* fix(vr): harden deferred FSR recovery

Rationale:
Deferred dispatch must preserve temporal reset intent after a skipped
frame or source-cache invalidation. Valid foveated host subregions must
remain usable, and a readiness-only wait must not select host fallback
for later runtime work in the same engine frame.

Implementation:
Re-arm history reset in deferred submit and main-pass paths, sharing the
submit helper with replay. Resolve host readiness from the full dispatch
plan so subregions retain bounds and exact lifecycle-contract checks.
Latch host selection in dispatch instead of readiness queries. Strengthen
production-source regression cases for provider selection, host bounds,
ownership, real failures, and invalid inputs; document validation limits.
Builds, tests, and hooks remain unrun at the user's explicit direction.

* docs(vr): record PR75 NVIDIA tuning comparison

Rationale:
PR75 needs measured timing and full-history health evidence against its
main-VR base. Preserve successful and interrupted attempts separately so
terminal passes cannot hide recovered failures or missing measurements.

Implementation:

retry and profiler details in the canonical ledger. Add the relevant
main-VR reference and prior PR75 interruption to the older PR ledger
without changing existing historical cells. Preserve all 66 candidate
transitions and descriptive pass means and standard errors.

Document the lower observed mean, resolved fidelity/fallback findings,

pull_request_body:
## Why

FSR can return Pending during cold activation or temporary provider
resource waits.
When submit-input freshness rejects stereo batching, the single-eye path
currently collapses that readiness wait into a failed evaluation if no
compatible host fallback exists.

This is the code mechanism consistent with the recovered failures at
transition 26 (DLSS Hoshipa to FSR3 Hoshipa) and transition 28 (None to
FSR3 Ultra Performance) reported after #65 and in the #66 candidate.
The exact internal wait in those historical frames was not retained.

This is an independent repair against `main-VR`, intended to land before
#66 after validation.

## What changed

- Carry Ready, Deferred, and Failed through single-eye FSR, foveated,
  main-pass, and submit replay dispatch.
- Present ordinary stretch for deferred submit work and hold the
  compositor cycle on presentation-only output. Restore a cleared
  admission record after intermediate texture recreation without
  overwriting another cycle or contract.
- Avoid publishing incomplete output, recording failed evaluation, or
  arming foveated failure backoff for Deferred. Deferred submits preserve
  history-reset intent even after source-cache invalidation. Main-pass
  deferral also retains reset intent after a skipped warm frame.
- Reuse the host-fallback readiness policy with the complete dispatch
  plan. Admit valid foveated subregions within context bounds while
  retaining exact display-contract checks during lifecycle deferral.
- Select a frame's host fallback only when a dispatch takes that route.
  A readiness-only wait can recover to runtime dispatch if its gate
  clears during the same engine frame.
- Add `FSREyeDispatch` controller coverage using extracted production
  functions and the deferred-presentation helper with dependency
  doubles; document behavior and outstanding qualification.

## Runtime and failure behavior

Producer freshness checks still govern peer reads and stereo batching.
Pending provider setup/evaluation keeps compatible host fallback eligible;
lifecycle admission fences continue to defer dispatch. Host-readiness
checks retain the actual dispatch guard when a lifecycle gate changes
between foveated admission and provider evaluation.
Actual provider/device failures retain failure and quarantine handling.
DLSS retains its existing success/failure classification. Flat SE/AE
FSR also propagates Deferred to the existing main-pass lifecycle path.

The tests exercise selected production single-eye/stereo functions,
resource-compatibility checks, the resolver's gate-selection block, and
the presentation helper with dependency doubles. They do not execute the
full resolver/submit/main-pass integration or a graphics runtime.

commit_message:
fix(upscaling): keep VR encoder reads eye-local (#66)

* fix(upscaling): keep VR motion donors eye-local

Rationale:
The packed-stereo input encoder bounded neighborhood reads only against
the combined texture extent. Near the center seam, DLSS motion selection
and HMD mask-edge probes could therefore sample the peer eye. Foveated
dispatches must still retain valid same-eye donors outside their crop.

Implementation:
Publish inclusive/exclusive full-eye X bounds through the existing
constant-buffer padding, and apply a shared predicate to both
neighborhood readers. Keep flat rendering full-width, add GPU
regressions for cropped 5x5 footprints, and validate every runtime VR
encoder variant.

* refactor(upscaling): fold VR source-bound checks

Rationale:
The first eye-bound predicate appended two X comparisons to the existing
physical texture checks. FXC duplicated that avoidable work across the
unrolled DLSS donor footprint even though host-published eye bounds are
already contained by the source texture.

Implementation:
Use unsigned half-open interval tests to combine each lower and upper
bound into one comparison. Preserve all sampling behavior and texture
reads while matching the parent instruction counts for default and FSR
variants and reducing the DLSS shader by ten instruction slots.

* ci(shaders): validate flat encoder variants

Rationale:
The shared upscaling encoder serves flat rendering as well as VR, but
only VR runtime permutations were registered for compilation. Its bounds
helper also needs an explicit full-eye interval contract for reviewers.

Implementation:
Add default, DLSS, FSR, and FSR depth-output flat runtime permutations
and run them through the existing shader CI matrix. Cover bare FSR in
the VR matrix too, document both configurations, and add concise Doxygen
documentation without changing the bounds predicate.
pull_request_body:
## Why

At the packed-stereo seam, the upscaling encoder could read depth and
motion data from the other eye. Both DLSS's motion-vector donor search
and the HMD mask-edge probe need bounds for the admitted source eye.
Foveated dispatch crops must still allow valid donors elsewhere in that
same eye.

## What changed

-   Publish each complete source eye's half-open X interval on both VR
    encoder paths; flat rendering publishes the complete texture width.
-   Apply one bounds predicate to the HMD mask-edge probe and the 5x5 DLSS
    motion-vector search, preserving valid donors outside foveated crops.
-   Test both eyes, physical texture edges, rejected peer-eye samples,
    and accepted same-eye samples beyond foveated dispatch crops.
-   Compile default, DLSS, FSR, and FSR depth-output encoder permutations
    for flat and VR rendering through the runtime shader-validation matrix.

## Integration and compatibility

Rebased onto `main-VR` at
`7c8e3e6568972f0dfbae83d60e3b6d2cbd68bc99`, including merged PR #65.
The final diff is limited to nine encoder, test, and validation files.

PR #65's producer-freshness admission, eye-selection checks, ownership,
fallback behavior, telemetry, and PuddleMask correction remain intact.
The only additions to `Upscaling.cpp` are the three bounds assignments.
The constant buffer remains 64 bytes, with its bounds member at byte 56.

The obsolete PuddleMask warning-budget commit and unrelated MSVC tooling
commit have been removed from this PR. The tooling work is preserved
separately in [PR #74](https://github.com/ParticleTroned/skyrim-community-shaders/pull/74).
No NVIDIA SDK or Streamline implementation changes are included. The
existing HAM shader, dispatch geometry, and donor ranking are unchanged.
The bounds guard adds no texture reads, dispatches, or candidate samples.

commit_message:
build(devbench): make main-thread waits determinate (#68)

* build(devbench): make DevBench waits determinate

Rationale:
DevBench bridges could time out after a queued main-thread action had
already won execution, report failure, and then mutate runtime state
later. That makes retry decisions unsafe and contradicts the command
result.

Implementation:
Use the shared main-thread dispatch state across the affected bridges.
Queued work can be cancelled before admission; admitted work publishes
its exact result before the caller returns. Cover cancellation,
admission, and exception propagation with deterministic controller
tests.

* build(devbench): centralize determinate dispatch

Rationale:
Duplicated dispatch paths must agree about admission and submission
errors. A queue may retain or start its callback before throwing, so
reporting a terminal failure without cancellation can hide a later
runtime mutation.

Implementation:
Cancel retained callbacks before reporting submission failure and
preserve exact results after admission. Share the admission protocol and
existing error envelopes across DevBench bridges and the screenshot
service. Cover dispatch races, binding exceptions, wire responses, and
dispatch-header coexistence.

* build(devbench): preserve dispatch template compatibility

Rationale:
The result-state template is an existing interface used by independent
bridge changes. Renaming it breaks those callers, while its name
collides with the lightweight claim phase enum when both headers are
included.

Implementation:
Keep MainThreadDispatchState as the result template and rename the claim
phase enum to MainThreadDispatchPhase. Retain joint-header compatibility
without changing dispatch behavior.

* build(devbench): make menu dispatch determinate

Rationale:
The menu DevBench bridge retained the original load-then-cancel race, so
a mutating main-thread action could begin after its caller reported a
timeout. That contradicted the determinate admission contract applied to
peer bridges.

Implementation:
Route menu actions through the shared admission and completion helper.
Queued actions now cancel atomically, admitted actions return their
exact outcome, and existing standard error responses remain unchanged.

## Why

A DevBench request could report a timeout while its main-thread task had
already won admission and could still change runtime state. That made a retry
unsafe: the caller was told that work had failed even though the original
mutation might still complete.

## What changed

- Make queued cancellation and task admission one mutex-serialized decision.
- Once admission wins, wait for and return the exact result or established
  failure response instead of reporting a false timeout.
- Share the protocol across editor, feature, profiler, shader, weather,
  performance, menu, and screenshot bridges, plus the screenshot service.
- Cancel a retained callback before reporting queue-submission failure; if a
  callback already ran or was admitted, preserve its actual result.
- In the migrated result-bearing helpers, bind runtime thread affinity inside
  the admitted task's exception guard, so cancelled work has no binding side
  effect and binding failures become the existing response form.
- Preserve the standard, profiler, and screenshot wire-error envelopes through
  one adapter.
- Give the lightweight render-scale dispatch phase enum a distinct name so it
  coexists with the result-state template. The render-scale admission and
  in-progress contract is otherwise unchanged.

The branch is rebased without conflicts onto `main-VR` commit
`358069e8fc2294fc5dce2a94a97997423dfe3c34`, including merged PR #67. Each of
the four original commits retains its author name, email, and author date.
Their source changes are preserved; rewritten messages use the release-neutral
`build(devbench)` type and explicit rationale/implementation sections.

## Failure and compatibility behavior

The five-second deadline bounds queue admission, not action execution. A
callback cancelled while queued is permanently ineligible. If admission wins
the race, the caller remains attached until the action returns or throws; this
prevents an unreported late mutation. A callback that never finishes can
therefore retain its caller.

Submission failure, action exceptions, thread-affinity binding exceptions,
missing task interfaces, and unknown failures remain observable through their
established response families. The shared result-bearing helper adds no
polling, retry loop, global registry, or frame-path work; it is used only at
DevBench request boundaries. The shared protocol applies to SE, AE, and VR.

Two preserved claim-based alternatives in the upscaling and render-scale paths
keep their existing in-progress semantics. A delayed callback cancelled before
admission cannot execute its domain action, although it may still perform the
pre-existing runtime-affinity binding first. Those alternatives remain outside
this PR's result-bearing dispatch changes.

fix(shader-cache): preserve safe shader reuse (#71)

* fix(shader-cache): preserve compatible records

Rationale:
Upstream has the managed pack container but still rejects whole cache
sets for seed ABI changes, keys compatible external ranges as exact
versions, and can fall back to thousands of loose files from a partial
installation.

Implementation:
Integrate the reviewed managed-pack safety lineage and the corrected
compatibility contract on current upstream main-VR. Retain multiple
exact record versions under stable compatibility domains, version
feature shader contracts, emit exactly six managed root files, and fail
partial managed layouts closed to source-only compilation.

* fix(shader-cache): guard pack mutation ownership

Rationale:
Overlapping A/B stores could share a writer, and exceptional mutations
could expose partially updated indexes or retain provisional ownership.

Implementation:
Lease each physical pack member, share guarded admission, and retain the
store lock through exception cleanup before reporting diagnostics.
Reject duplicate and decreasing record sequences while preserving valid
prefixes. Cover overlapping process writers and failed append
publication.

* fix(shader-cache): preserve scoped runtime compatibility

Rationale:
Invalid managed layouts must survive cache lifecycle actions, and warm
records must retain complete source dependencies through hot reload.
Horizon compatibility must reflect the active Water integration without
changing unrelated shader identities.

Implementation:
Protect invalid layouts from legacy rebuild and rotation paths.
Serialize source invalidation with complete closure traversals and
preserve tracking when reads fail. Register the Horizon provider only
for the loaded feature and delegate its ABI to that Water contract.
Reject ambiguous canonical inputs, share requirement serialization, and
enable both cache tests' assertions in Release builds.

* build(shader-cache): validate runtime and horizon packages

Rationale:
The universal core's display-version suffix cannot identify the SE/AE
cache slot. Consolidated packs must retain both Horizon variants and
validate the same storage and compatibility contract as the runtime.

Implementation:
Use pack runtime metadata, enforce the six-file inventory, ABI
agreement, and required Horizon declarations. Share lane definitions and
align text, version, and sequence validation with C++. Honor explicit
empty feature ABIs and verify Water separation and non-Water
deduplication. Exercise SE/VR archives and explain automatic Horizon
selection in the FOMOD.

* docs(shader-cache): clarify SE/AE and Horizon installs

Rationale:
The cache runbook must explain the shared desktop cache and Horizon
selection, and accurately describe managed failure and ownership rules.

Implementation:
Document the SE/AE versus VR cache slots, shared core version labels,
Horizon ABI ownership and restart behavior, runtime qualification
matrix, per-member writer leases, strict sequences, and source-only
recovery.

* fix(shader-cache): pin compiled shader provenance

Rationale:
Deferred writes and feature-set commits could label older bytecode with
newer source contents or settings, allowing an incompatible cache hit.

Implementation:
Retain source, compile-state, lane, and owning blob snapshots through
persistence. Verify the source closure with fresh post-compile reads and
keep bytecode memory-only when verification fails. Add asserted native
regressions for same-timestamp edits, read failures, and digest
retention.

* build(shader-cache): validate selected runtime packages

Rationale:
Manifest declarations alone admitted caches without actual Horizon
coverage, and development FOMOD generation always required SE/AE input.
Unicode line separators also produced different offline domain digests.

Implementation:
Share canonical record identities between emission and export
validation. Check visible paired variants and content contracts,
preserving appended coverage. Add default-on SE/AE inclusion with an
explicit VR-only flag. Preserve literal Unicode fingerprint bytes and
extend packaging tests.

* ci(shader-cache): allow VR-only manual FOMOD builds

Rationale:
Manual FOMOD generation needs to skip SE/AE compilation and packaging
when preparing VR development artifacts.

Implementation:
Expose default-on SE/AE inclusion for manual dispatch and carry the
choice through cache generation, download, assembly, and archive checks.
Keep both runtimes for automatic releases and include the compatibility
catalog in the assembler checkout for export validation.

* docs(shader-cache): record adversarial review and usage

Rationale:
Reviewers and cache builders need the confirmed fixes, Horizon design
history, runtime choices, and limits of the available validation.

Implementation:
Document captured compilation provenance, actual variant coverage, and
VR-only CLI and workflow generation. Record inspected branch identities,
retained Horizon installation rules, regression evidence, and the
remaining in-game qualification boundary.
