pull_request_body:
## Why

Managed shader packs must retain reusable records across compatible
provider updates and reject incompatible records without discarding the
installation. Deferred writes could mislabel compiled bytecode, and
package declarations could promise Horizon support without corresponding
shader records. Development FOMOD builds also need a VR-only option.

## What changed

- Separate container admission from record compatibility. Treat manifest
  ABI as seed provenance and retain versions under stable provider domains
  with declared minor-version compatibility ranges.
- Preserve source closures, compile settings, global/feature ABIs, provider
  major versions, resource fingerprints, and scopes in record identity.
- Lease physical pack members to exclude overlapping A/B writers and
  hard-link aliases. Hold mutation locks through cleanup and withdraw
  authority after uncertain append, compaction, or reset state.
- Align C++ and Python rejection of ambiguous canonical inputs and
  duplicate/decreasing sequences, including Unicode fingerprints.
- Track includes for warm hits and synchronize closure reads with reload
  invalidation. Retain captured source, compile-state, lane, and owning
  bytecode snapshots through queued writes and feature-set commits.
  Changed or unverifiable post-compile inputs leave the blob memory-only.
- Share record identity construction between emission and export checks.
  Validate canonical metadata, DXBC signatures, paired permutations,
  common content contracts, and an actual Water bytecode difference.
  Empty packs and relabeled standard records cannot prove Horizon support.
- Add default-on SE/AE inclusion to the FOMOD CLI and manual release
  workflow. Retain both runtimes for automatic releases and include the
  compatibility catalog in the sparse packaging checkout.
- Keep assertions enabled in Release cache regression targets.

Rebased onto `main-VR` `8f89c1f9d`, including PR70. All nine original
authors/dates are preserved. The resulting tree equals Git's clean merge
of the previous PR head with that base. The cache implementation and
packaging code are unchanged by this rebase; 28 of 31 PR files are byte
identical, while CMake, startup logging, and the runbook retain base changes.

## Runtime and failure behavior

The `SE` cache serves SE and AE; VR has its own permutation inventory and
compile state. Runtime comes from `PackManifest.json.runtime`, not the
universal DLL's display-version suffix. Test-build display identity stays
separate from compatibility markers.

Each included runtime carries standard and Horizon-compatible Water
records together. The frozen registry activates Horizon only when the
companion DLL and CSX feature are active. Water owns that provider ABI;
unrelated records remain shared. Provider/feature changes require restart.
The FOMOD offers explicit VR, SE/AE, and no-cache choices on one page.

For a VR-only development package:

```powershell
python tools/build-fomod-package.py --core <aio-root> --vr-cache <vr-cache-root> --no-include-se-ae --output <new-output> --version <version>
```

This omits the SE/AE input requirement, payload, installer option, and
mapping. Combining `--se-cache` with the exclusion flag is rejected.
VR still requires both Horizon states. Manual **Release: Build Artifacts**
exposes the same default-on `include-se-ae` choice.

Invalid or inaccessible managed layouts fall back to source compilation
without regenerating loose files or destroying installed members. Loose
caching remains available without a managed installation. Incompatible
records miss narrowly; compaction may retire historical entries. Release
exports additionally require complete paired coverage. This PR adds no
HLSL rendering change or HorizonFix companion DLL.

## Validation

Fresh checks on the rebased candidate:

- `pwsh ./tools/cmake.ps1 -S ../pr71-review-evidence-20260910/controller-project -B ../pr71-review-evidence-20260910/controller-build -G "Visual Studio 18 2026" -A x64`

  passed with MSVC 19.51, C++23, `/W4`, and assertions enabled. MSVC reports
  the expected `/DNDEBUG` override from `/UNDEBUG`.
- `ctest --test-dir ../pr71-review-evidence-20260910/controller-build -C Release --output-on-failure --no-tests=error --timeout 120`:
  source provenance, compatibility registry, and all three packaging suites
  passed. Two native pack checks failed under restricted Windows access.
- `ctest --test-dir ../pr71-review-evidence-20260910/controller-build -C Release --verbose --no-tests=error --timeout 120 -R '^ShaderCachePack'`:
  passed with normal Windows access, including both failed pack checks and
  the packaging suite. All seven distinct focused CTest entries therefore
  pass. Pack tests cover native writer exclusion/failures and C++/Python
  interoperability against the shared 29-case corpus.
- Python suites: FOMOD **30/30**, shader-cache packaging **20/20**, release
  workflow **3/3**. These include archive extraction/staging/repacking,
  full and VR-only packages, seven event/input combinations, embedded
  PowerShell syntax, and sparse-checkout archive assembly.
- `python ../pr71-review-evidence-20260910/check_rebase.py`: passed exact
  merge-tree equality, all nine author names/emails/dates, wrapped commit
  bodies, base ancestry, retained base changes, `git diff --check`, and

  attempt was rate-limited. This review found no additional code change
  warranted by the rebase or focused regressions.

The previous head `9a3a9248a` had passed the universal Release plugin build.

release cache generation, and hosted workflow execution were not performed

fix(vr): preserve submit and relatch ownership (#73)

Rationale:
VR submit-stage upscaling needs consistent stereo inputs and color
contracts. Render-scale changes also need exact provider ownership so
completed drains avoid unnecessary settling without weakening fallback.
Preserve the complete measurement history as the next optimization base.

Implementation:
Freeze stereo temporal metadata at world post-processing and bind it to
vendor dispatch. Preserve input ownership, fallback color and frame-token
publication. Observe provider drain readiness without teardown; advance
only the owning retry and commit after the native stereo callback.
Require consumed provider proofs and published target identity before
guard exemption, retaining preparation and promotion revalidation.

Expose lifecycle timings through DevBench and retain controller coverage.
Include accumulated render-scale reports, iteration guidance, comparison
tooling and SteamVR helpers. Store the complete record as three numbered
plain CSV snapshots below 100 MiB and retain raw evidence
locally. Balance the historical partitions and pin PR65/PR66 baselines
with the latest PR73 measurement. Require a new immutable numbered ledger
per measurement, containing only that PR's measurements and selected
baselines. Add cross-partition audits and reject snapshot overwrites.
Suppress oversized ledger text diffs while preserving ordinary CSV data.
Exclude the separate PBR fix.

Validation:
The retained NVIDIA assay completed 33/33 transitions in both passes,
with mean strict times of 815.09/768.53 ms, 62/62 stretch frames and 15/15
retries. The complete summary and both comparisons reconstruct from the
ledger, including 528 candidate timing cells and unchanged history.
Existing universal DevBench ON/OFF builds, controller and shader checks
passed. The frame-zero regression, 24 ledger tests, nine SteamVR fixture
cases and staged pre-commit checks passed during merge preparation.
Live failure injection, SE/AE runtime and visual release qualification
remain unrun. Memory and formal improvement assessments are inconclusive.

## Why

VR submit-stage upscaling needs stable stereo input and color contracts.
Render-scale changes also need exact provider ownership so a completed
drain can avoid unnecessary settling while retaining safe fallback.

## What changed

- Capture immutable stereo camera, jitter, timing and reset metadata at
  the world post-processing boundary; bind it to vendor/foveated dispatch.
- Keep input freshness and COM ownership checks. Auto/Gamma retain temporal
  admission; Linear uses spatial presentation. Preserve fallback color and
  Streamline token publication when dispatch fails.
- Observe provider drain readiness without teardown or mutation. Advance
  only the owning Backend retry, within its original six-frame window,
  and commit after the complete native stereo callback returns.
- Require consumed old-provider proofs, cleanup ownership and published
  target identity for guard exemption. Revalidate during preparation and
  promotion; retain coherent stereo and next-cycle release requirements.
- Expose drain, consumption, publication, preparation and eligibility
  timings through DevBench without new GPU polling.
- Preserve the accumulated render-scale reports and complete record in
  three numbered CSVs. Balance the historical archives and retain PR65/PR66
  baselines with the latest PR73 run. Require each future measurement to
  create an immutable numbered ledger scoped to its PR and baselines.
  Include comparison tooling and SteamVR helpers with fixture coverage.
  Suppress oversized ledger text diffs while retaining ordinary CSV storage.

## Runtime and failure behavior

The frozen metadata and stereo callback scope apply to VR; SE/AE retain
their ordinary rendering paths. Missing, stale, failed or mixed ownership
falls back to conservative settling. Device loss does not admit destructive
work. Detached retirement ownership is not proof of fence completion.
The earlier whole-transaction retry acceleration remains reverted.

Measured PR73 source **`554e484e3`** (Build `e7e9fa2d13f2`, main-VR

each, Dragonsreach, runtime-only settings, fixture `0.3/0.3/0.7`.

- **Execution and health:** 66/66 completed; 66 terminal PASS. Task 2 counts
  are 66 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 INCONCLUSIVE. Device-loss, OOM, producer-terminal,
  vendor-native qualification and credible liveness-timeout counts are
  each zero. No counted lifecycle, fidelity, retirement or fallback failures;
  no recovery reset was needed. Captures are inactive and evidence is flushed.
- **Stretch:** all 32 selected stretch transitions recovered, with no active
  tail. Full-pass stretch is 62 frames in each pass, down from 69 / 78.
  Raw cumulative acceptance remains false: the fixed two-frame cutoff is
  diagnostic during imposed settling, and the scaled-only presentation
  gate conflicts with proven native terminal presentation. Both applicable
  health standards are MET; those raw gate results remain preserved.
- **Retries:** 15 per pass versus 9 / 10. Each new pass has four DLSS viewport
  retries and eleven relatch requeues. More retries coexist with shorter
  retry-to-stable intervals; that interval includes subsequent settling
  and is not isolated retry overhead.
- **Optimization targets:** owned drain Pending→Ready takes one frame

fix(pbr): synchronize material registries

Rationale:
PBR culling queries share metadata maps with material loading and
removal. Unprotected mutation can corrupt concurrent lookup and matches
the reported CommunityShaders crash.

Implementation:
Encapsulate both registries with shared lookup and exclusive mutation.
Copy metadata and claim MATO ownership atomically, reject removed MATO
entries, and exclude unregistration during editor visits. Keep engine
calls outside registry locks, skip empty landscape slots, and use atomic
one-time diagnostics. Add eight lifecycle and concurrency scenarios and
preserve the crash investigation, review findings, and build provenance.

build(tooling): retain active MSVC installation (#74)

Rationale:
Repairing a partial MSVC environment must keep the active Visual Studio
installation instead of mixing compiler and SDK state from another one.
Unavailable active paths must allow discovery, and test probes must
restore variable presence as well as inherited values.

Implementation:
Prefer an explicit VsDevCmd override, then a valid active installation,
then discovery. Check the active path before joining its child paths.
Restore complete test snapshots with environment-provider deletion and
assert exact restoration. Preserve initialized-environment reuse and
cover partial repair, invalid overrides, and incomplete installations.
Document selection and fallback behavior.

Validation:
Fresh and initialized MSVC probes compiled standard-library headers.
Success and expected-failure paths restored the process environment.
Missing-drive and cleanup regressions failed before their fixes and
passed afterward. Scoped pre-commit and git diff --check passed.

## Why

Repairing a partial MSVC environment can select a different Visual
Studio installation from the one already active, mixing compiler and
SDK state and failing before compilation.

## What changed

Prefer a valid active `VSINSTALLDIR` after an explicit `CSX_VSDEVCMD`
override and before installation discovery. Check that the active path
exists before joining child paths so an unavailable drive can fall back
to discovery.

Restore the tooling test's complete process environment before the real
compiler probe and in its cleanup path. Remove newly introduced
variables through the environment provider: setting them to `$null`
through .NET can leave empty variables on current PowerShell versions.
Assert exact snapshot restoration, including variable presence.

Rebased onto `main-VR` at `b2021de91a16f271d3ce1383168fdc523724074c`.
Resolved the test conflict by retaining both the base's initialized
environment reuse regression and the partial-environment repair probe.
Original commit authorship and author date are preserved.

## Failure behavior and scope

- Missing paths, unavailable drives, and installations without
  `VsDevCmd.bat` or MSVC tools fall back to discovery.
- An invalid explicit override still fails with its diagnostic.
- A complete inherited MSVC environment is reused without reinitializing.
- Changes are confined to the shared build helper, its test, and tooling
  documentation. Game runtime and shader sources are unchanged.

The adversarial review found and fixed the unavailable-drive failure and
incomplete environment cleanup. Existing resolver and environment
patterns were reused. GitHub had no CodeRabbit review threads or inline
findings; its only comment reported that automatic review was skipped.

## Validation

- `pwsh -NoProfile -File tests/tool_environment_test.ps1`: passed after
  rebase. The expanded suite also passed through the fresh and

## Why

existing configurations.

## What changed

- Add five validated, persisted controls, disabled by default: velocity

  frame and minimum disocclusion accumulation.
- Expose enable, edit, apply and restore through the Upscaling menu and
  `communityshaders.fsr_temporal_tuning` on SE, AE and VR.
- Apply all five controls through one runtime FSR3/FSR4 configuration
  path, including FSR 4.1.1. There is no provider-version allowlist;
  actual configure results determine complete-profile acceptance.
- Capture one requested profile for every context before dispatch.
  Atomic revisions defer newer edits to safe context recreation and
  preserve the same profile between sequential eye dispatches.
- Share numeric definitions across validation, persistence, live patches
  and the DevBench input schema. Reject invalid live patches atomically
  and isolate malformed saved profiles from unrelated settings.
- Report requested and applied settings, pending/rejected/faulted status,
  provider identity and `configurationApplied` from actual acceptance.

remain unchanged.

adjustment lets DLSS/DLAA users tune sharpening during movement with

## What changed

- Add a default-disabled motion adjustment, threshold in output pixels
  per rendered frame, and strength cap for both DLSS/DLAA sharpeners.
  Negative adjustment reduces sharpening in moving areas; positive
  adjustment increases it within the cap.
- Share motion policy, per-eye/crop mapping, resource ownership, state
  restoration and fallback between RCAS and Luma. Luma retains its gain
  curve, luminance detail limit, chroma ratios and alpha.
- Expose the same controls for either sharpener in the menu and through
  `communityshaders.menu` action `set_motion_adaptive_sharpening`.

- Validate live JSON numbers before narrowing to floats. Normalize only
  the four optional persisted fields, using logged defaults for malformed
  values while preserving unrelated settings.
- Include both shaders in runtime validation and document the controls,
  compatibility, fallbacks and reference provenance.

## Safety and compatibility

The option remains off by default. Both fixed shaders retain identical
DXBC in the checked flat, VR, HDR and VR+HDR permutations. FSR keeps its
integrated sharpening. Zero base sharpness disables the sharpening pass.
The cap can also limit stationary pixels when below the base strength;
motion is measured per frame without frame-rate normalization.

Raw unjittered engine motion is mapped per eye/crop. Color and motion
reads stay inside the current region. Missing motion, invalid geometry,
reset/menu frames and shader/dispatch failures retain the selected fixed
sharpener. Nonfinite motion falls back per pixel, bypassing the optional
cap. Submit-stage motion requires a current producer proof.

The shared optional pass restores compute state through RAII and unbinds
the owned output before binding inputs, preventing overlapping UAVs from
silently suppressing input SRVs. Optional shaders preload when enabled
at setup; setup failure remains latched until the shader cache is cleared.
No extra color or motion textures are allocated. The implementation covers
flat SE/AE, packed VR and submit-stage eyes, including cropped/foveated
output. It does not change vendor contexts or history-reset policy.

no OptiScaler source was copied. OptiScaler's GPL-3.0 license is
acknowledged. Existing AMD RCAS copyright and MIT notices remain intact.
Pinned references are in `docs/development/motion-adaptive-sharpening.md`.

sharpeners. Their file-relative includes compiled with the earlier test
resolver but failed through `Util::CompileShader`, whose include resolver
starts at `Data/Shaders`. The corrected paths enable the intended adaptive
shader instead of silently retaining fixed sharpening. A garbled range

without changing its default root or resolution behavior. Review covered

shadow history and cursor state; unavailable shadow data keeps the
existing fully lit fallback. Preset scheduling remains unchanged.

## Why

Skyrim and Community Shaders share a D3D11 immediate context, but its
protection could be disabled when a screenshot or flowmap user finished.
VR loading messages also invoke a native UI clear that changes both D3D
state and the engine's renderer state outside the ordinary render path.
Observed concurrent writers support correcting these ownership contracts;
the complete sequence behind the earlier hang remains unproven.

## What changed

- Apply one durable context policy at both device-creation hooks and at
  renderer initialization. Preserve creation options except SINGLETHREADED,
  enable protection, and verify its resulting state.
- Keep screenshot and flowmap users on that policy. Execute private flowmap
  command lists with state restoration and avoid holding the context lock
  across texture loading, encoding or filesystem operations.
- Guard the VR loading-message clear with a nonblocking attempt to acquire
  the existing renderer critical section. Leave contended clears pending
  for the normal rendering path.
- Expose read-only graphics_context_status through DevBench, including API
  readiness, native guard admission and aggregate implementation readiness.
- Add native WARP and loading-menu admission tests, with focused ownership
  documentation. Driver probes and unrelated investigation fixes are
  excluded from this 14-file production change.

## Runtime and failure behavior

The D3D policy applies to SE, AE and VR. Failed protection releases and
clears successful creation outputs; an incompatible published context

## Why
Skylighting temporarily replaces the engine's precipitation render state.
Manual tail cleanup does not protect early exits or ordinary C++ unwinding.
Direction reconstruction also needs valid zenith inputs and protection
against floating-point roundoff near the horizon.

## What changed
- Save the original depth target, cube sizes, direction and occlusion flag
  before mutation, and restore them with the existing scope guard.
- Restore projection inputs before recomputing the camera projection.

- Clamp the hemisphere reconstruction radicand to zero.
- Normalize saved and edited zenith angles through the existing settings
  helper: finite values stay within 0–90 degrees; nonfinite values use the
  default. Direct slider entry is normalized immediately.
- Register a regression test that compiles the actual settings normalizer

fix(skylighting): invalidate history after loading (#95)

Rationale:
Save loading and environment transitions can leave Skylighting sampling
history from the previous scene. Repeated buffer publication and skipped
prepasses must retain pending rebuild work until it can actually run.

Implementation:
Queue invalidation atomically from loading events and environment changes,
clear graphics history on the render thread, and require a fresh occlusion
capture before sampling. Retain requests delivered during clearing.
Share resource readiness checks and keep the published feature buffer in
agreement with probe availability, including late invalidation. Commit
movement and full-update work only after dispatch. Preserve baseline
same-device target recreation and add production lifecycle regression
coverage for reset timing, resource recovery and dispatch cadence.
pull_request_body:
## Why
Loading a save or changing between interior and exterior environments can
leave Skylighting sampling history from the previous scene. Clearing the
probe volumes alone is insufficient: the next probe update must also use
a fresh occlusion capture.

Buffer publication can happen more than once per frame. It must not
consume rebuild work before a probe dispatch actually runs.

## What changed
- Queue invalidation directly from the existing post-load/new-game
  callback, loading-menu close, and render-thread environment transitions.
- Use one atomic queue method. Consume requests before clearing so an
  event delivered during a reset remains pending.
- Require a fresh occlusion capture after clearing probe history. Keep
  Skylighting disabled and its history SRVs unbound while invalidated.
- Share the resource-readiness check between buffer publication and the
  prepass. A successful capture cannot authorize a dispatch whose
  published feature buffer still has Skylighting disabled.
- When invalidation arrives after enabled buffer publication, refresh the
  existing feature buffer before unbinding the history SRVs.
- Commit probe movement and decrement forced full-update work only after
  dispatch. Repeated HDR buffer updates and skipped prepasses retain it.
- Add a controller test that compiles the actual lifecycle and probe-pass
  methods against recording graphics/engine substitutes.

## Compatibility and failure behavior
Loading callbacks only queue an atomic request; graphics clears remain on
the render thread. Missing context, shaders or resources leave work
pending and prevent sampling until the required inputs recover.

Existing SE/AE/VR hooks, history formats, user settings and device/grid
rebuild paths remain in use. Same-device target recreation retains its
baseline behavior; this PR adds no render-scale invalidation policy.

Adversarial review covered event timing, repeated buffer publication,
late invalidation, resource recovery, reset reentry and update cadence.
Shared readiness checks and the existing feature-buffer update path avoid
parallel implementations of those policies.

feat(vr): add OCU draw and gaze APIs (#82)

* feat(vr): add OCU draw and gaze APIs

Rationale:
OCU needs a supported boundary for DAPA mask draws and a versioned gaze
profile for optional peripheral effect sampling. These contracts avoid
depending on private CSX offsets or identifying compatible DLL hashes.

Implementation:
Expose synchronous accepted-draw observers with guarded single replay,
borrowed geometry state, quiescent unregister, and DevBench diagnostics.
Consume coherent OCU gaze snapshots for an opt-in VR AO/GI shader variant,
preserving native sampling on unavailable, stale, or invalid profiles.
Add ABI, lifecycle, policy, and shader tests and document game qualification.

* fix(vr): harden OCU fallback and draw attribution

Rationale:
An overflowed geometry restore can expose an unrelated parent draw, and
an optional OCU shader failure currently discards the native SSGI batch.
The new setting also needs a supported DevBench mutation for automation.

Implementation:
Invalidate unverifiable geometry scopes and compile optional variants
independently after committing the required shaders. Clear old optional
permutations, retain native fallback, and share define and hook bookkeeping.
Add a validated DevBench setter using the UI's setting/history transition,
limit the OCU constant buffer to VR, and document the public contracts.
Add production-code regression coverage for optional compiler failures,
96 permutations and setting lifecycle; reproduce both original defects.

Validation:
Five focused MSVC controller suites and two source contracts pass. Fourteen
universal syntax checks pass with DevBench enabled and disabled. Existing
unused template parameters require /wd4100 for Hooks and XSEPlugin.
All 72 native DXBC comparisons are identical, 36 OCU shaders compile,
mixed-version shaders fail closed, and D3D11 WARP buffer restoration passes.
Scoped hooks and formatting pass. No new linked DLL or live game run.

* fix(vr): harden OCU draw and query boundaries

Rationale:
Rejected shadow or reflection draws could claim the accepted-draw
rendering thread before scene-depth validation. An exception from the
optional OCU profile query could also terminate native rendering.
The remaining review comments require bounded tests and a valid API
query example.

Implementation:
Bind the rendering thread only after scene-depth qualification while
retaining early rejection for an already-bound foreign thread. Contain
provider query exceptions, expose the failure status, and recover through
the next frame's query with native sampling in the meantime.
Exercise production draw filtering and query failure recovery in focused
controller tests. Add the registry timeout and namespace-qualified API
example, and document the resulting lifetime and fallback behavior.

* docs(vr): record PR82 NVIDIA comparison

Rationale:
Preserve the requested comparison of the current main-VR test AIO
against the last measured PR73 build without attributing these results
to the unmeasured PR82 implementation.

Implementation:
Add an immutable two-run ledger, exact coverage receipt, complete
per-pass and transition reports, and index and iteration entries.
Preserve the baseline cells and separate terminal success from the
observed latency increase and inconclusive performance assessment.
Verify all 1,056 timing cells, complete summary reconstruction, physical
DLL identity, capture cleanup, and scoped pre-commit checks.

* docs(vr): record second NVIDIA comparison

Rationale:
Preserve the repeated render-scale measurement and make variation between
the latest PR73 baseline and both September 13 runs visible on PR82.

Implementation:
Add immutable ledger 0005 with all three summaries, both comparisons and
every retained timing. Record physical build identity, pacing diagnostics
and comparison limits. Show all three runs in the summary and transition
tables, using seconds for switch durations and full-pass stretch totals.

* docs(vr): record paced COC endurance results

Rationale:
Preserve the requested 25-transition COC test on the PR82 integration
build, including the limits of comparison with published PR73 evidence.

Implementation:
Add immutable ledger 0006 with complete results, per-transition timings,
capture details, retained gate failures and the historical COC reference.
Record all 25 strict passes, 12 recovered requeues and verified cleanup.
Document that PR73 setting-switch timings are not a COC loading baseline.

* docs(vr): clarify archived PR73 COC retries

Rationale:
The published PR73 setting-switch tables do not describe its separate
local COC attempts. Explain the surviving evidence so their absence
from the PR is not mistaken for an absence of COC testing.

Implementation:
Document the same Windhelm relatch retry in both exact-build archives
and distinguish unmeasured positioning from measured transitions.
Retain the crash and missing-receipt limits on any full-pass comparison.
Existing finalized measurements and immutable ledgers are unchanged.

* fix(vr): recover OCU mask delivery after loading

Rationale:
The accepted-draw provider retained its first scene thread for the
process lifetime. Gameplay on a different thread then stopped reaching
OCU even though registration succeeded.

Implementation:
Retire ownership at the VR completed-frame boundary and let the next
eligible scene draw claim it. Preserve within-frame filtering and
callback isolation, and cover repeated handoffs in the service test.
Document the frame lifetime without changing either public API.
Remove unrelated render-scale reports from the feature diff; their
original commits retain the measurements.

Seven focused tests and the Release DLL build passed. A Skyrim VR
headset retest reports working player masking with a small edge sliver
still visible. Full item coverage and performance remain unqualified.

## Why OCU needs supported CSX interfaces for DAPA ownership masks and optional gaze-driven effect sampling, without version-specific offsets. ## What changed - **DAPA:** provide accepted-draw API v1 through `CSX_GetAcceptedDrawAPI` and `csx.render.accepted_draw`. Deliver attributed indexed and indexed-instanced lighting/effect draws with single-use mask replay. OCU classifies player bodies, equipment, held arrows, crossbow props, HIGGS-held objects and other owned meshes through its existing consumer. - **Loading recovery:** retire draw-thread ownership at the completed frame boundary. The next eligible scene draw can claim the new thread, preventing delivery from remaining stuck on the loading thread. - **Eye foveation:** consume OCU's independent v1 gaze snapshot for optional SSGI peripheral sampling. Include diagnostics, integration documentation and focused regression tests for both interfaces. ## Compatibility and failure behavior The draw provider is VR-only. Scene-depth filtering, within-frame thread ownership, callback isolation and synchronous replay remain enforced. Consumer ownership rules and both public v1 contracts are unchanged by the loading-recovery fix. SSGI peripheral sampling defaults off. Missing, stale or invalid gaze, provider exceptions and optional shader failures retain native sampling. This does not change vendor upscaler parameters or DAPA pacing. The loading-recovery fix changes no shaders or shader-cache compatibility. ## Validation - Seven focused CTest cases passed: AcceptedDrawRegistry, AcceptedDrawService, OCUEffectFoveationPolicy, OCUEffectFoveationClient, OCUEffectIntegration, PresetCompatibility and FeaturePresetCompatibilityContract. The service regression covers repeated frame-boundary thread changes, within-frame rejection, shadow filtering, wrong contexts and callback isolation. - Full Release ALL (SE/AE/VR) DLL build and link passed. Deployed DLL identity, unchanged export names, no additional imported DLLs and unchanged shader-cache ABI were verified. - Skyrim VR headset retest: the tester reports that player masking now works and looks good; a very small outline/sliver remains visible. This is user-observed visual validation, not exhaustive item coverage. - Remaining qualification: the edge sliver, all ownership categories across equip/load transitions, live gaze loss/recovery, and controlled CPU/GPU measurements. No performance gain or complete SE/AE runtime qualification is claimed. ## NVIDIA health and comparison with PR73 The baseline is PR73's last documented run, **554e484e39** (Build **e7e9fa2d13f2**). The new run is clean post-merge **main-VR 54e99dde36** (Build **82d114cc62b0**), run ID `nvidia-20260914T074354211Z`. This render-scale switching assay does not establish live coverage of PR82's accepted-draw or OCU gaze APIs. Each run used two ordered 33-transition passes in one Skyrim VR game process, Dragonsreach, five-second server pacing, runtime-only API settings, and foveation 0.3/0.3/0.7. The new run used the verified NVIDIA RTX 5070 Ti Laptop GPU producer DLL. Both position receipts identify the same Dragonsreach cell and exact player position; the tester confirms the interior fixture was fixed. PR73 had no startup-active VR FPS Stabilizer upscaling profile sync, while the new run did. After positioning, PR73 reported DLSS Quality with Render Scale on; the new run reported DLAA with Render Scale off. The assay applies its own transition targets, but this startup-state difference makes settings drift a plausible contributor to frame cadence. - **Execution and health:** the new run completed 66/66 transitions, with 66 terminal PASS and Task 2 counts of 66 PASS / 0 FAIL / 0 INCONCLUSIVE. Both applicable pass health standards are MET. Device loss, OOM, producer-terminal failure, vendor-native qualification failure, and credible liveness timeout are zero. No counted lifecycle, fidelity, retirement, or fallback failure; no recovery reset. Captures are inactive and the evidence journal is flushed. The reporting status is COMPLETE. - **Switch latency versus PR73:** mean strict durations are **0.815 s / 0.769 s** for PR73 and **0.928 s / 0.871 s** for the new run, **+13.90% / +13.32%**. The new run is slower on 31/33 and 30/33 routes in passes 1 and 2. These descriptive differences do not isolate the effect of PR82's changes. - **Stretch and retries:** all 33 selected new-run stretch transitions recovered. Full-pass stretch is **64 / 62 frames**, **4.799 / 4.650 s**, versus PR73's **62 / 62 frames** and **4.081 / 4.085 s**. No active tail remains. Retries are **15 / 15**, with 4 / 4 viewport retries and 11 / 11 relatch requeues. These are recovered observations, not counted failures. - **Largest slowdowns versus PR73:** pass 1 row 6 +463.06 ms, row 17 +298.81 ms, row 24 +249.28 ms; pass 2 row 15 +277.29 ms, row 14 +209.41 ms, row 20 +206.30 ms. The transition table retains each route and both passes. - **Pacing diagnostic:** worker pacing was VALID; maximum client dispatch gap was 52.63 ms against the 250 ms budget. The preceding five-second wait is outside each measured strict-completion interval. - **Limits:** formal improvement-or-neutral assessment is INCONCLUSIVE. The automated context check sees different adapter LUID, game-time/ weather metadata, and dependencies. Cell and position match, and the tester confirms the fixed interior fixture. Fixture fingerprints and a versioned tolerance policy are unavailable. Both applicable health standards are MET. The fixed stretch cutoff remains a diagnostic during imposed settling; the scaled-only presentation gate is a contract mismatch for proven native terminal presentation. Raw false cumulative acceptance is retained. pull_request_body:
## Why

Recent SSGI and VR upscaling source changes invalidated the pinned
runtime settings fingerprint. The unified-preset generator therefore
stopped `validate` before checking the generated packages.

## What changed

Pin the reviewed source-tree hash and regenerate the three preset
compatibility markers and the deterministic evidence report. Preset
values, the base snapshot, package version, and contract revision 5
remain unchanged.

## Contract review

Since the previous policy pin, the covered changes are in
`ScreenSpaceGI.cpp/.h` and `Upscaling.cpp/.h`. The new VR-only SSGI
experiment is absent from the pinned base, and its defaulting loader
sets it to `false`; no preset migration or required JSON path changed.
Upscaling preserves the existing `false` mask-preview value on load.
`VRRenderScaleDevBenchBridge.cpp` also changed, but is not in the
settings-source inventory and does not contribute to this hash.

The runtime checks the marker revision and SHA-256 syntax, not equality
with its own source tree. The source hash records generator provenance;
keeping revision 5 does not relax the loader's compatibility check.

## Validation

- `pwsh -NoProfile -File tools/generate-unified-presets.ps1 -Check`
  passed for all three tiers.
- `pwsh -NoProfile -File tests/unified_preset_generator_test.ps1`
  passed (the `validate` workflow command).
- An independent comparison found each tier identical to `main-VR`
  after replacing only the fingerprint marker. All three report hashes
  match the generated files' SHA-256 values.
- `pwsh ./tools/pre-commit.ps1 run` passed on staged files.
- `pwsh ./tools/git.ps1 diff --check` passed.

commit_message:
feat(adaptive-balance): tune sky and water

Rationale:
Sky saturation and water caustics/parallax need native profile controls
without duplicating the existing lighting and color pipeline. Base wave
amplitude and weather response are complementary and should be grouped
so their combined effect is clear.

Implementation:
Add bounded, neutral-default sky and water settings to Adaptive Balance
serialization, profile composition, transitions and shared shader data.
Place sky saturation in Lighting, caustics and parallax in Water, and
group base amplitude with wind enable and calm/strong-wind scales.
Preserve existing wind composition and VR foveated parallax, and share a
guarded flowmap direction before division. Expose validated partial Global
updates and effective values through DevBench. Extend regression cases
and documentation; refresh preset compatibility hashes without changing
their settings, base or contract revision.

Validation:
Passed 82 shader preprocessing variants, 36 interpreted flowmap cases,
CPU/HLSL layout and DevBench contract checks, preset generator checks,
scoped formatting and diff checks. C++ regression fixtures extract
successfully. No C++/shader compilation or runtime validation was run.

## Why

releases and hot reloads. Incomplete managed installations must compile

commit_message:
fix(vr): prevent cyclic shadow submissions

Rationale:
VR can freeze indefinitely when cached shadow render passes form a cycle
in the native batch links. A copied shadow dispatch order can also replay
work withdrawn while an earlier light renders. Preserve light and sun
lifetime safety while following native live dispatch and batch lifetime.
The captured cycle proves corruption, not its writer or introducing PR.

Implementation:
Select each shadow light from the live accumulated order and retain only
its current owner through Render. Validate non-owning owner-location
hints under the queue lock and release ownership outside it. Retain the
scene for its directly owned sun instead of taking an intrusive sun ref.

Give lightless Utility shadow submissions stable per-batch pass copies,
retain their geometry and property, and deduplicate identical membership.
Retire records only after native bucket drain/reset and defer reclamation
until native readers finish. Keep native drawing and final owner release
outside new locks. Use the verified VR map layout and one checked
transaction for seven runtime/version/byte-validated hooks; leave SE/AE
installation unchanged.

Reduce bookkeeping with a weak renderer cache invalidated on destruction,
a stable bucket cache and one membership insertion lookup. Grow dense
membership off to the side so allocation failure cannot corrupt existing
submissions; preserve capacity for allocation-free warmed operation.

Validation:
Universal SE/AE/VR Release DLL builds. Eight focused controller tests pass,
including production installer rollback, renderer-address reuse, populated
allocation failures and ownership/reentrancy cases. All hook prefixes
match preserved live bytes. Scoped formatting and whitespace checks pass.

Nine alternating synthetic benchmark pairs reduce isolation bookkeeping
by 15-20%; at 4096 submissions the median changes from 0.286 to 0.243 ms.
These are mock-native registration/drain costs, not game-frame timings.

In-game submission counts (2026-09-21):
WhiterunExterior01, PID 11228: five disjoint 300-frame windows yielded
1,500 complete, coherent samples and 2,031,181 protected submissions.
Mean 1,354.121/frame; median 1,373; P95 1,400; minimum/maximum 1,237/1,412.
Duplicates, allocation failures, unwound calls and rejected windows: zero.
Player position and feature settings matched between reads; HMD pose was
not recorded. This is sampled frame coverage, not a continuous capture.

The measured source was c610f1690452aef65ff28bf64435fded53b3ca35 plus
DevBench-only counters, with verified embedded producer Build ID:
bc07aa988fb12802d1dd448816b5dbc233c430291999946fccbf446504f0568b
The physical enabled-mod DLL hash was not re-resolved during the read.

Modeled CPU cost at the observed submission count:
Before bookkeeping correction: 0.091-0.095 ms/frame.
Current shadow-submission protection: 0.073-0.080 ms/frame.
Estimated saving: 0.014-0.018 ms/frame.
These values scale the prior 512/4096-submission microbenchmarks; they
are not directly measured in-game timings, confidence bounds or total
PR96 costs. The earlier roughly 0.3 ms synthetic result assumes 4,096
submissions and must not be labeled this scene's per-frame overhead.
Counting adds synchronization, so its frametimes were not used.

Preserve exact producer identity, frame windows, calculation and limits
in docs/development/vr-shadow-admission-cost-review.md. Counting code,
tests and build registration remain separately stashed; production
contains no added counting instrumentation.

Matched in-game performance, shadow fidelity and freeze testing remain
pending. Retain the investigation and explicit evidence limits in docs.

commit_message:
fix(volumetric-lighting): restore godray colour controls

Rationale:
Godray colour tuning can miss the colour consumed by final composition,
and the CPU gamut constraint prevents HDR saturation above neutral.
Apply the selected context's settings to the engine-resolved colour so
the controls affect both VR and flat rendering consistently.

Implementation:
Upload sanitized saturation and custom colour through the shared buffer
and tune the final volumetric composite independently of lens flare.
Preserve intensity, opacity, weather records and neutral context gating.
Remove obsolete CPU colour helpers, reuse shader luminance utilities,
and invalidate the feature shader ABI. Use precise weighted blending to
retain dark custom colours against bright HDR weather and bitwise finite
checks to preserve neutral opacity fallback under shader optimization.
Compress saturation at the half-float range limit without losing
luminance, including bright weather colours near the format maximum.

Add WARP tests of the actual optimized VR and SE/AE shaders, including
buffer layout, saturation, custom colour, invalid inputs and lens flare.
Exercise production profile selection and upload code across exterior,
sunlit and sunless interiors, disabled settings and non-world passes.
Share reflected test-buffer utilities with the skylighting regression.
Refresh preset compatibility fingerprints without changing settings.

Universal SE/AE/VR Release DLL build passed. CTest passed all three
focused tests: VolumetricLightingTuningPolicy, VolumetricLightingComposite
and SkylightingProbeSlice. All six composite permutations passed.
